### Quick Reference additions (Cycle 22)

| Symptom | Likely Root Cause | Pattern/Fix | Anti-Pattern to Avoid |
|---------|-------------------|-------------|----------------------|
| `vi.spyOn` mock persists to next test — original not called | `restoreMocks` not enabled | Pattern 120 (`restoreMocks: true` + `resetMocks: true` in config) | AP60 (`restoreMocks` without `resetMocks`) |
| `vi.fn()` mock returns previous test's value in next test | `resetMocks` not enabled | Pattern 120 (`resetMocks: true` in config) | AP60 (only `restoreMocks` enabled) |
| Test fails with "element is covered" — non-deterministic overlay appears | Cookie/signup banner blocks actionability | Pattern 121 (`page.addLocatorHandler()` with `times` option) | Hardcoded `waitForTimeout` to skip overlay |
| Flaky test passes on retry but CI shows green — flakiness silently accumulates | No `failOnFlakyTests` gate in CI | Pattern 122 (`failOnFlakyTests: !!process.env.CI` + quarantine split) | AP61 (navigation handler without post-handler URL accounting) |
| Page hangs waiting for UI — `clock.install()` used for date-only freeze | `install()` freezes `setTimeout`; polling loop never fires | Pattern 123 (use `clock.setFixedTime()` for date-only scenarios) | Using `clock.install()` when only `Date` freeze is needed |
| Timer fires after test ends — corrupts next test's mock call count | Leaked `setTimeout` not cleared | Pattern 124 (`detectAsyncLeaks: true` surfaces exact source location) | AP62 (enabling leak detection on suites with intentional background workers) |
| `detectAsyncLeaks` warnings all point to `node_modules` — noisy | SDK async resources initialized per-test | Move SDK init to `globalSetup`; use `afterAll` for teardown | Disabling `detectAsyncLeaks` entirely to avoid noise |
| `addLocatorHandler()` causes random timeouts in long test cases | Handler execution time counted against action timeout | Increase action `timeout` option; use `noWaitAfter: true` in handler | Gotcha 61 (complex handler animation + low action timeout) |

### Pattern 125 — Playwright `testInfo.retry`-Gated Cleanup for Safe State Reset on Re-Run  [community]

When a test is retried it inherits leftover server-side or database state from the failed attempt.
A guard on `testInfo.retry` lets the before-hook perform a destructive reset only on retry runs,
keeping the first attempt fast and avoiding double-write errors.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — retries enabled only in CI
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
export default defineConfig({
  retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,
  use: { trace: 'on-first-retry' },
});

// fixtures/db-cleanup.ts
import { test as base, TestInfo } from '@playwright/test';

export const test = base.extend<{ dbCleanup: void }>({
  dbCleanup: [async ({ request }, use, testInfo: TestInfo) => {
    if (testInfo.retry > 0) {
      // Only perform expensive teardown when retrying — keeps first attempt lean.
      await request.delete('/api/test-data', {
        data: { runId: testInfo.title },
      });
      console.log(`[retry ${testInfo.retry}] cleaned up state before re-run`);
    }
    await use();
    // Always clean up after the final attempt.
    await request.delete('/api/test-data', {
      data: { runId: testInfo.title },
    });
  }, { auto: true }],
});

// usage in test file
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/db-cleanup';
test('order submission persists correctly', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit Order' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByText('Order confirmed')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** The guard introduces branching in fixture code. Document it clearly — teams unfamiliar
with `testInfo.retry` will be confused why cleanup is conditional. The cleanup DELETE must be
idempotent (safe to call even when no data exists from a previous run).

---

### Pattern 126 — Jest `retryTimes` with `logErrorsBeforeRetry` and `waitBeforeRetry` for Targeted Async Retry  [community]

Jest's built-in retry is often used without the `logErrorsBeforeRetry` option, which silences
the error output from failed attempts and makes flakiness root-cause analysis impossible in CI.
Combining all three options — count, logging, and delay — gives the maximum signal per retry.

```typescript
// __tests__/flaky-network.test.ts
import axios from 'axios';

// Declare at describe-level, NOT inside a test — jest.retryTimes must be top-level.
// logErrorsBeforeRetry: true logs each failure to stdout, enabling CI log search.
// waitBeforeRetry: 500 — pause between retries reduces thundering-herd to a shared service.
// retryImmediately: false (default) — don't skip other queued tests while retrying.
jest.retryTimes(3, { logErrorsBeforeRetry: true, waitBeforeRetry: 500 });

describe('Payment gateway integration', () => {
  test('charge endpoint returns 200 within SLA', async () => {
    const response = await axios.post('/api/charge', {
      amount: 100,
      currency: 'USD',
      token: 'tok_visa',
    });
    expect(response.status).toBe(200);
    expect(response.data.chargeId).toMatch(/^ch_/);
  });

  test('refund endpoint is idempotent', async () => {
    const refund = await axios.post('/api/refund', { chargeId: 'ch_test' });
    expect(refund.data.status).toBe('succeeded');
  });
});
```

**Key constraint:** `jest.retryTimes` applies to every test in the file (or describe block if
nested). Avoid setting high retry counts at file level — prefer quarantine tags over blanket
retries, and treat `retryTimes` as a temporary scaffold while diagnosing root cause, not a
permanent fix.

### Pattern 127 — Playwright `test.fixme()` Quarantine with Tracking Annotation  [community]

`test.fixme()` immediately aborts the test without running it (unlike `test.skip()` which is
identical but semantically means "intentionally excluded"). Using `test.fixme` with a structured
annotation links every quarantined test to a tracked issue, creating an audit trail that prevents
"forgotten quarantine" syndrome.

```typescript
// tests/checkout.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Checkout flow', () => {
  // test.fixme with issue annotation — shows in HTML reporter and JSON output.
  // The test IS executed (to verify the fix) but reported as "fixme" not "failed".
  test('coupon code applies correct discount', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
    testInfo.annotations.push({
      type: 'quarantine',
      description: 'Flaky: timing race in coupon validation — tracked in JIRA-4821',
    });
    test.fixme(true, 'JIRA-4821: coupon endpoint has 200ms race; quarantined 2026-05-13');

    await page.goto('/checkout');
    await page.getByLabel('Coupon code').fill('SAVE10');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply' }).click();
    await expect(page.getByText('10% discount applied')).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('order total recalculates after quantity change', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout');
    await page.getByLabel('Quantity').fill('3');
    await expect(page.getByTestId('order-total')).toContainText('$');
  });
});
```

**Why `fixme` over `skip`:** `test.fixme` signals intent-to-fix, appears distinctly in the HTML
reporter, and still executes the test body so you can observe whether the underlying issue has
been resolved. `test.skip` hides the test entirely. Reserve `skip` for permanently inapplicable
tests (browser/OS combinations); use `fixme` for known defects awaiting resolution.

---

### Pattern 128 — Vitest `retry` Config with Per-Suite Override via `test.each`  [community]

Vitest's `retry` config option sets a project-wide default. For test suites that contain a mix
of deterministic and inherently non-deterministic tests (e.g., real DB integration vs pure unit),
you can override at the `describe` level using `test.each` with per-case retry metadata injected
through a custom fixture, keeping the retry scope as narrow as possible.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    // Default: no retries for unit tests.
    retry: 0,
    // Log every retry attempt for CI traceability.
    // Vitest prints the attempt number and error before each re-run.
  },
});

// tests/integration/db-pool.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from 'vitest';
import { getDbConnection } from '../../src/db';

// Integration tests touching a shared dev DB can be transiently flaky.
// Override retry count at describe level with test.extend or by passing
// the retry option directly on each flakiness-prone test case.
describe('database connection pool', () => {
  test(
    'acquires and releases connections under concurrent load',
    async () => {
      const results = await Promise.all(
        Array.from({ length: 10 }, () => getDbConnection().query('SELECT 1'))
      );
      expect(results).toHaveLength(10);
      results.forEach((r) => expect(r.rows[0]).toEqual({ '?column?': 1 }));
    },
    // Vitest test options: { retry, timeout, repeats }
    { retry: 2, timeout: 10_000 }
  );

  test('rejects when pool is exhausted', async () => {
    // Pure logic test — no retry needed; failure here is always deterministic.
    const pool = getDbConnection({ maxConnections: 0 });
    await expect(pool.query('SELECT 1')).rejects.toThrow('pool exhausted');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Per-test retry options are not visible in test names or HTML reports unless you
add a manual annotation. Teams scanning the test file won't know some tests retry silently.
Add a comment block beside each `{ retry: N }` option explaining WHY the retry exists and
which issue it covers.

---

### Pattern 129 — Playwright `testInfo.status` vs `testInfo.expectedStatus` for Custom Post-Test Teardown Logic  [community]

After a test completes (or is retried), the `afterEach` hook receives both `testInfo.status`
(what actually happened) and `testInfo.expectedStatus` (what was expected). Comparing these
lets you perform different teardown actions — e.g., capture a full-page screenshot and dump
network logs only on unexpected failures, not on intentional `test.fail()` cases.

```typescript
// fixtures/smart-teardown.ts
import { test as base, TestInfo } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

export const test = base.extend({});

test.afterEach(async ({ page }, testInfo: TestInfo) => {
  const unexpectedFailure =
    testInfo.status !== testInfo.expectedStatus &&
    testInfo.status === 'failed';

  if (unexpectedFailure) {
    // Capture state for flakiness investigation — only on genuine failures.
    const screenshotPath = path.join(
      testInfo.outputDir,
      `failure-${testInfo.retry}.png`
    );
    await page.screenshot({ path: screenshotPath, fullPage: true });
    testInfo.attachments.push({
      name: `failure-screenshot-retry-${testInfo.retry}`,
      contentType: 'image/png',
      path: screenshotPath,
    });

    // Dump active network requests to aid async timing diagnosis.
    const requestLog = (page as any)._requestLog ?? [];
    const logPath = path.join(testInfo.outputDir, `network-${testInfo.retry}.json`);
    fs.writeFileSync(logPath, JSON.stringify(requestLog, null, 2));
    testInfo.attachments.push({
      name: `network-log-retry-${testInfo.retry}`,
      contentType: 'application/json',
      path: logPath,
    });
  }
});
```

**Why this matters for flakiness:** Teams that capture screenshots for ALL failures (including
expected `test.fail()` outcomes and retried-then-passed runs) generate gigabytes of CI artifacts
that obscure the real failures. Gating on `status !== expectedStatus` keeps the signal clean.

---

### Pattern 130 — Playwright `page.route()` with Abort for Eliminating Third-Party Script Flakiness  [community]

Third-party scripts (analytics, chat widgets, A/B testing SDKs) are a major source of E2E
flakiness: they introduce unpredictable network latency, hydration errors, and interfere with
actionability checks. Blocking them in test environments removes an entire class of non-determinism.

```typescript
// fixtures/block-third-party.ts
import { test as base, Page } from '@playwright/test';

// Domains whose scripts are known flakiness sources in E2E tests.
const BLOCKED_DOMAINS = [
  '*.segment.io',
  '*.intercom.io',
  '*.hotjar.com',
  '*.fullstory.com',
  '*.optimizely.com',
  '*.googletagmanager.com',
];

async function blockThirdPartyScripts(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await page.route('**/*', (route) => {
    const url = route.request().url();
    const isBlocked = BLOCKED_DOMAINS.some((pattern) => {
      const regex = new RegExp(pattern.replace('*', '.*'));
      return regex.test(url);
    });
    if (isBlocked) {
      route.abort('blockedbyclient');
    } else {
      route.continue();
    }
  });
}

export const test = base.extend<{ blockThirdParty: void }>({
  blockThirdParty: [async ({ page }, use) => {
    await blockThirdPartyScripts(page);
    await use();
  }, { auto: true }],
});

// tests/landing.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/block-third-party';
test('hero CTA is visible without third-party interference', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Get started' })).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Blocking analytics scripts means your E2E suite cannot verify that analytics
events fire correctly. Keep a separate "analytics smoke" project that does NOT use this fixture
and runs against staging with real network access.

---

### Pattern 131 — Vitest `pool: 'vmForks'` Isolation Mode for Module-Level Singleton Flakiness  [community]

Module-level singletons (database connection pools, config caches, event emitters initialized
at module load time) are a hidden source of parallel test flakiness. Vitest's `vmForks` pool
creates a fresh Node.js VM context per worker, ensuring each worker gets a clean module registry
without the overhead of spawning child processes.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    // vmForks: fresh VM context per worker = module-level singletons are isolated.
    // Use when: you have module-level side effects (DB pools, config caches, logger init).
    // Avoid when: tests share expensive setup (use 'threads' + beforeAll isolation instead).
    pool: 'vmForks',
    poolOptions: {
      vmForks: {
        // Limit concurrent VMs to avoid OOM in CI with large module graphs.
        maxForks: 4,
        // Reuse VMs across test files in the same shard for better performance.
        singleFork: false,
      },
    },
    // Still run file-level parallelism — vmForks provides module isolation,
    // not serial execution.
    fileParallelism: true,
  },
});

// Example singleton that causes flakiness with 'threads' pool:
// src/config.ts
let _config: Record<string, string> | null = null;
export function getConfig(): Record<string, string> {
  if (!_config) {
    _config = { apiUrl: process.env.API_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000' };
  }
  return _config;
}
// With vmForks, each worker sees _config = null at startup — no shared mutation.
```

**Tradeoff:** `vmForks` is slower than `threads` because it cannot share native module bindings
across VM contexts. Benchmark your suite: if startup time increases by more than 20%, prefer
`threads` pool with explicit singleton reset in `beforeEach` instead.

---

### Pattern 132 — GitHub Actions `test-reporter` Matrix Aggregation for Per-Test Flakiness Visibility  [community]

GitHub Actions workflows that shard tests across multiple runners produce one JUnit XML artifact
per shard. Without aggregation, flakiness trends are invisible — a test that fails in shard 3
and passes in shard 1 looks like a one-off rather than a recurring issue. Using
`dorny/test-reporter` with `merge-multiple: true` consolidates all shards into a single
annotated check run.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/e2e.yml
name: E2E Tests
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false   # Don't cancel sibling shards on one failure
      matrix:
        shardIndex: [1, 2, 3, 4]
        shardTotal: [4]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20' }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: npx playwright test
          --shard=${{ matrix.shardIndex }}/${{ matrix.shardTotal }}
          --reporter=junit
        env:
          PLAYWRIGHT_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE: results/shard-${{ matrix.shardIndex }}.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: playwright-results-${{ matrix.shardIndex }}
          path: results/shard-${{ matrix.shardIndex }}.xml

  report:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: playwright-results-*
          merge-multiple: true   # Combines all shard XMLs into one directory
          path: results/
      # dorny/test-reporter annotates each failing test directly on the PR.
      - uses: dorny/test-reporter@v2
        with:
          name: Playwright E2E Results
          path: results/*.xml
          reporter: java-junit
          fail-on-error: false   # Let the test job itself control pass/fail
```

**Community signal:** Teams that skip the aggregation step report "alert fatigue" — CI shows
green because individual shard failures are below the threshold, but the same test consistently
fails across weekly runs in different shards. The `merge-multiple` pattern surfaces this
cross-shard pattern.

---

### Pattern 133 — `AbortController`-Based Test Timeout Guards for Promise-Hanging Async Tests  [community]

Tests that await long-running Promises without a timeout can hang indefinitely in CI, consuming
worker slots and blocking the entire suite. An `AbortController`-based wrapper races the actual
operation against a deadline and throws a descriptive error when the deadline expires — far more
useful than Vitest's generic "test timed out" message.

```typescript
// utils/with-timeout.ts
export function withTimeout<T>(
  promise: Promise<T>,
  ms: number,
  label: string
): Promise<T> {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), ms);

  return Promise.race([
    promise.finally(() => clearTimeout(timer)),
    new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
      controller.signal.addEventListener('abort', () => {
        reject(
          new Error(
            `[withTimeout] "${label}" exceeded ${ms}ms. ` +
            `Check for missing await, unresolved promise, or hung event listener.`
          )
        );
      });
    }),
  ]);
}

// tests/websocket.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from 'vitest';
import { withTimeout } from '../utils/with-timeout';
import { createWsClient } from '../../src/ws-client';

describe('WebSocket message delivery', () => {
  test('receives message within 2s SLA', async () => {
    const client = createWsClient('ws://localhost:8080');

    const message = await withTimeout(
      new Promise<string>((resolve) => {
        client.on('message', (data: string) => resolve(data));
        client.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'ping' }));
      }),
      2_000,
      'WebSocket ping-pong'
    );

    expect(JSON.parse(message).type).toBe('pong');
    client.close();
  });
});
```

**Why this beats test-level `timeout`:** Vitest's `timeout` option kills the test after N ms
but the error message just says "exceeded timeout". The `withTimeout` wrapper produces an error
message that names the specific operation that hung, making the flakiness root cause immediately
obvious in CI logs without needing to reproduce locally.

---

### Pattern 134 — Playwright `context.isClosed()` Guard in Long-Running Fixture Teardown  [community]

Fixtures that perform HTTP cleanup calls after a test completes can throw `BrowserContext has
been closed` errors if the context is already torn down when the fixture's `finally` block runs.
This is especially common with test timeouts and `test.abort()`. Guarding with
`context.isClosed()` makes teardown unconditionally safe.

```typescript
// fixtures/authenticated-context.ts
import { test as base, BrowserContext, APIRequestContext } from '@playwright/test';

interface AuthFixtures {
  authedContext: BrowserContext;
}

export const test = base.extend<AuthFixtures>({
  authedContext: async ({ browser, request }, use) => {
    // Create context and authenticate via storage state.
    const storageState = await getStorageState(request);
    const context = await browser.newContext({ storageState });

    try {
      await use(context);
    } finally {
      // Guard: context may already be closed if test was aborted or timed out.
      if (!context.isClosed()) {
        // Revoke server-side session token before closing.
        try {
          await context.request.delete('/api/sessions/current');
        } catch {
          // Swallow teardown-only errors — they don't affect test result.
        }
        await context.close();
      }
    }
  },
});

async function getStorageState(request: APIRequestContext) {
  const response = await request.post('/api/auth/login', {
    data: { username: 'e2e-user', password: process.env.E2E_PASSWORD },
  });
  return response.json();
}
```

**Why this matters for flakiness:** Without the `isClosed()` guard, the `DELETE /api/sessions`
call throws an unhandled error in the fixture teardown, which Playwright surfaces as a test
infrastructure error rather than a test failure. This creates ghost failures — tests that
passed but show an error in the report — causing teams to rerun tests unnecessarily.

---

### Pattern 135 — pytest `--randomly-seed` Capture and Artifact Upload for Reproducible Order-Dependent Failures  [community]

Python test suites using `pytest-randomly` shuffle execution order per run. When an
order-dependent failure is caught in CI, the default workflow loses the seed after the run
completes. Capturing the seed as a CI artifact and exposing it as a step output enables
deterministic reproduction without re-running the entire suite.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/python-tests.yml
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: '3.12' }
      - run: pip install pytest pytest-randomly pytest-rerunfailures
      - name: Run tests and capture seed
        id: pytest-run
        run: |
          # pytest-randomly prints "Using --randomly-seed=<N>" to stdout.
          OUTPUT=$(python -m pytest tests/ -v --tb=short 2>&1 | tee /dev/stderr)
          SEED=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -oP '(?<=--randomly-seed=)\d+' | head -1)
          echo "seed=${SEED}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "pytest_output<<EOF" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "$OUTPUT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "EOF" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Upload seed artifact
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pytest-seed
          path: |
            # Write seed to file for easy artifact download.
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Annotate PR with reproduction command
        if: failure()
        run: |
          echo "### Reproduce order-dependent failure" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "\`\`\`bash" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "python -m pytest tests/ --randomly-seed=${{ steps.pytest-run.outputs.seed }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "\`\`\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
```

**Community signal:** Teams without seed capture spend 30–60 minutes per flaky CI failure
trying to reproduce locally with `--randomly-seed=0` (fully random), often failing to hit the
same order. With seed capture, the first local reproduction attempt succeeds 100% of the time.

---

### Pattern 136 — Trunk AI Auto-Quarantine with Ownership Ticketing and Infection-Model Circuit Breaker  [community]

AI-powered flakiness platforms (Trunk, Launchable, Buildkite Test Engine) automatically
quarantine flaky tests in CI without code changes. The quarantined test continues executing
(for signal collection) but its failure is suppressed from blocking merges. The key operational
pattern is coupling quarantine with automatic ticket creation and an infection-model circuit
breaker that halts new quarantines when the flaky test count exceeds a threshold.

```typescript
// scripts/quarantine-circuit-breaker.ts
// Run as a GitHub Actions step BEFORE the main test job.
// Reads Trunk quarantine API; blocks CI if quarantine count exceeds threshold.
import * as core from '@actions/core';

const QUARANTINE_API = 'https://api.trunk.io/v1/flaky-tests/quarantine';
const MAX_QUARANTINED = 15; // Infection model: > 15 quarantined = systemic problem

async function checkQuarantineHealth(): Promise<void> {
  const response = await fetch(QUARANTINE_API, {
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.TRUNK_API_TOKEN}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
  });
  const data = (await response.json()) as { quarantined: { id: string; name: string }[] };

  const count = data.quarantined.length;
  core.info(`Quarantined test count: ${count}/${MAX_QUARANTINED}`);

  if (count >= MAX_QUARANTINED) {
    core.setFailed(
      `[Circuit Breaker] ${count} tests are quarantined (limit: ${MAX_QUARANTINED}). ` +
      `Merge is blocked until at least ${count - MAX_QUARANTINED + 1} quarantined tests ` +
      `are fixed and removed from quarantine. See: https://app.trunk.io/flaky-tests`
    );
  }
}

checkQuarantineHealth().catch((err) => core.setFailed(String(err)));
```

**Tradeoff:** Auto-quarantine without a circuit breaker creates a false-safety illusion: the
CI stays green while product quality degrades silently. The infection-model threshold (Pattern 53
in earlier cycles) is the essential counterbalance — it makes the accumulated debt visible and
blocks new merges when the flaky test backlog grows past a sustainable level. The threshold
should be set per-team based on velocity: small teams (≤ 5 engineers) set it at 5–10;
larger teams at 15–20.

---

### Pattern 137 — Playwright `route.fetch()` + Response Mutation for Deterministic API Response Testing  [community]

Tests that rely on a real upstream API returning specific data (e.g., a specific user's cart
contents) are prone to environment drift: test data is deleted, seeds are reset, or the API
returns a different shape after a schema migration. Using `route.fetch()` to pass the real
request through but mutate the response gives the best of both worlds — the real network path
is exercised (catching auth, routing, TLS issues) while the response body is deterministic.

```typescript
// tests/cart.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('cart total updates when item quantity changes', async ({ page }) => {
  // Intercept the cart API and mutate the response to a known fixture.
  await page.route('**/api/cart', async (route) => {
    const realResponse = await route.fetch();
    const body = await realResponse.json();

    // Overwrite items with deterministic fixture while preserving auth/headers.
    const mutated = {
      ...body,
      items: [
        { id: 'sku-001', name: 'Widget', quantity: 2, unitPrice: 9.99 },
        { id: 'sku-002', name: 'Gadget', quantity: 1, unitPrice: 24.99 },
      ],
      total: 44.97,
    };
    await route.fulfill({
      status: realResponse.status(),
      headers: Object.fromEntries(realResponse.headers()),
      json: mutated,
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/cart');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-total')).toHaveText('$44.97');

  // Change quantity for Widget — assert recalculation.
  await page.getByLabel('Widget quantity').fill('3');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-total')).toHaveText('$54.96');
});
```

**Key gotcha:** `route.fetch()` creates a new network request from the Playwright worker, not
from the browser context. If the API uses `Authorization` headers derived from the browser's
session (cookies vs. `Authorization: Bearer`), the fetched request may return a 401. Always
inspect `realResponse.status()` before fulfilling — if it's 4xx, fall back to a pure
`route.fulfill()` with a static fixture.

---

### Pattern 138 — `--sequence.shuffle.seed` in Vitest CI + Seed-Committed `vitest.workspace.ts` for Multi-Project Order-Dependency Detection  [community]

In monorepos with multiple Vitest projects (`vitest.workspace.ts`), test order-dependency bugs
most often occur at project boundaries: a test in `packages/api` leaves a module-level side
effect that corrupts a test in `packages/web`. Enabling shuffle with a stable seed per CI run
(derived from git commit SHA) exposes cross-project dependencies while remaining reproducible.

```typescript
// vitest.workspace.ts
import { defineWorkspace } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineWorkspace([
  {
    extends: './packages/api/vitest.config.ts',
    test: {
      name: 'api',
      root: './packages/api',
    },
  },
  {
    extends: './packages/web/vitest.config.ts',
    test: {
      name: 'web',
      root: './packages/web',
    },
  },
]);

// vitest.config.ts (root — applies to all workspace projects)
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

const CI_SEED = process.env.GITHUB_SHA
  ? parseInt(process.env.GITHUB_SHA.slice(0, 8), 16)  // Stable per-commit seed
  : undefined;  // Undefined = random seed locally (exposes more flakiness)

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    sequence: {
      shuffle: {
        files: true,   // Shuffle file order within each project
        tests: true,   // Shuffle test order within each file
      },
      seed: CI_SEED,
    },
  },
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Using git SHA as the seed means the same commit always produces the same order.
This is intentional for reproducibility. The failure mode to avoid: teams that set
`seed: 12345` permanently get reproducibility but lose the "expose new order dependencies"
benefit that random seeds provide. Use `seed: undefined` locally and SHA-derived seeds in CI.

---

### Pattern 139 — Playwright `expect(fn).toPass()` with Custom Back-Off Intervals for Polling-Based Flakiness Elimination  [community]

Some application state changes happen through background jobs, WebSockets, or eventual
consistency — the UI updates only after an asynchronous side effect completes. Using a
bare `expect(locator).toHaveText()` with a high timeout is wasteful. `expect(fn).toPass()`
with custom `intervals` implements exponential back-off, checking frequently at first then
slowing down, matching real-world job completion distributions.

```typescript
// tests/export.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('CSV export job completes and download link appears', async ({ page, request }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports');

  // Trigger the export — this kicks off a background job.
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export to CSV' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByText('Export queued')).toBeVisible();

  // Poll for completion with exponential back-off.
  // intervals: [500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 4000, 4000] — retries at these delays.
  // Total budget: 500+1000+2000+4000+4000+4000 = 15.5s before toPass throws.
  await expect(async () => {
    const status = await request.get('/api/exports/latest');
    const body = await status.json();
    expect(body.status).toBe('completed');
    expect(body.downloadUrl).toMatch(/^https:\/\//);
  }).toPass({
    intervals: [500, 1_000, 2_000, 4_000, 4_000, 4_000],
    timeout: 20_000,
  });

  // Now assert the UI reflects the completion.
  await page.reload();
  await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Download CSV' })).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Why this beats `waitForTimeout(15000)`:** The back-off intervals mean a fast job (completes
in 600ms) is detected at the 1,000ms interval — the test finishes in ~1s rather than 15s.
The test is also self-documenting: the `intervals` array communicates the expected job
completion distribution to anyone reading the code.

---

### Anti-Patterns (Cycle 24)

#### AP63 — Using `jest.retryTimes()` Inside a `beforeEach` Hook  [community]
**What:** Calling `jest.retryTimes(3)` inside a `beforeEach` block to apply different retry
counts to different test cases.
**Why harmful:** `jest.retryTimes()` is a file-level or `describe`-level declaration processed
at parse time by jest-circus. Calling it inside `beforeEach` does not scope retries to the
next test — it modifies the global retry count for all subsequent tests in the file, causing
unpredictable retry behavior. Tests later in the file inherit the last `retryTimes` value set
in any `beforeEach`. **Fix:** Use `jest.retryTimes()` only at the top level of a file or at
the top of a `describe` block.

#### AP64 — `page.route()` Handlers That Call `route.fetch()` After Context Close  [community]
**What:** Registering a `page.route()` handler that calls `route.fetch()` (to pass the request
through to the real server) and then not unregistering the handler before `context.close()`.
**Why harmful:** If a background request fires during or after context teardown (e.g., a polling
interval that fires at the same moment the test ends), `route.fetch()` is called on a closed
context and throws `APIRequestContext has been disposed`. This surfaces as an unhandled
promise rejection that corrupts the test result of the NEXT test case, not the current one.
**Fix:** Call `await page.unrouteAll({ behavior: 'wait' })` in `afterEach` before context
teardown, or use `route.fulfill()` with a static response instead of `route.fetch()` for
handlers where pass-through is not essential.

#### AP65 — Setting `retry: 2` in `vitest.config.ts` Globally Without a `retry.condition`  [community]
**What:** Configuring `retry: 2` (or `retry: { count: 2 }`) as a project-wide default in
`vitest.config.ts` to "fix" a suite that has some flaky tests.
**Why harmful:** Every deterministic failure (wrong assertion, missing mock, type error) now
runs three times before showing as failed. A suite that previously surfaced a broken test in
10 seconds now takes 30 seconds. More critically, the retry obscures the fact that the test
is consistently broken — developers may not notice the test is always failing because it shows
as "passed (after 2 retries)" in some reporters. **Fix:** Use `{ retry: N }` as a per-test
option on known flaky tests only, or use Vitest's `retry.condition` to limit retries to
transient error patterns (e.g., `ECONNRESET`, `timeout exceeded`).

---

### Real-World Gotchas (Cycle 24)  [community]

**Gotcha 63 — `route.fetch()` Returns a Different Response Shape After a Schema Migration**  [community]
Teams using `route.fetch()` to pass requests through and assert on the live response discover
that the test silently changes behavior after a backend schema migration. Because `route.fetch()`
hits the real server, the response JSON keys or types change — the test may pass because the
assertion only checks one field, but other assertions on fields that were renamed now silently
skip (if using optional chaining) or fail with a confusing type error rather than a clear
assertion failure. Fix: in tests that use `route.fetch()` for response mutation (Pattern 137),
always add a `expect(body).toMatchObject({ ...requiredShape })` assertion on the raw response
before mutating, to detect schema drift early.

**Gotcha 64 — `--randomly-seed=0` in pytest Does NOT Use a Fixed Seed**  [community]
Teams trying to reproduce a shuffled failure locally run `pytest --randomly-seed=0` expecting
a deterministic order, but seed `0` is treated by `pytest-randomly` as "use a random seed"
(same as omitting the flag). The correct way to use a specific seed is `--randomly-seed=<N>`
where N is the numeric seed captured from the failing CI run. This behavior is documented but
routinely confused with `--randomly-seed=last` (which re-uses the seed from the previous local
run). Capture the seed from CI output, not from `--randomly-seed=0`.

**Gotcha 65 — Playwright `tracing: 'on-first-retry'` Generates No Trace When `retries: 0` Is Set**  [community]
Teams configure `trace: 'on-first-retry'` in `playwright.config.ts` expecting traces to be
generated for all flaky tests. On local runs and in environments where `retries` defaults to 0,
no trace is ever generated — the "on first retry" condition never triggers because there are
no retries. When debugging a flakiness report from CI, developers who set `retries: 0` locally
(for speed) find that `trace: 'on-first-retry'` generates no useful output. Fix: use
`trace: 'retain-on-failure'` for local debugging sessions, and reserve
`trace: 'on-first-retry'` for CI where `retries: 2` is always set.

| Symptom | Likely Root Cause | Pattern/Fix | Anti-Pattern to Avoid |
|---------|-------------------|-------------|----------------------|
| Retry attempt leaves DB state that breaks next attempt | No `testInfo.retry` guard in cleanup fixture | Pattern 125 (`testInfo.retry > 0` conditional reset) | Unconditional destructive cleanup on every run |
| CI log shows "test passed" but same test fails next week | `logErrorsBeforeRetry` not set — silent retry | Pattern 126 (`jest.retryTimes(3, { logErrorsBeforeRetry: true })`) | AP63 (`retryTimes` inside `beforeEach`) |
| Quarantined test has no issue link — forgotten indefinitely | `test.fixme` with no annotation | Pattern 127 (`testInfo.annotations.push` + `test.fixme` + JIRA link) | `test.skip` for fixable flaky tests |
| Module-level singleton causes cross-worker state pollution | `threads` pool shares module registry | Pattern 131 (`vmForks` pool for module-level side effects) | AP65 (global `retry: 2` without condition) |
| Flaky shard failure not visible in PR checks | No JUnit XML aggregation across shards | Pattern 132 (`dorny/test-reporter` + `merge-multiple: true`) | Single-shard XML with no aggregation |
| `Promise` hangs in CI — no useful error message | No deadline guard on async operation | Pattern 133 (`withTimeout` wrapper with operation label) | `test.timeout` with generic timeout message |
| `BrowserContext has been closed` in fixture teardown | No `context.isClosed()` guard | Pattern 134 (`isClosed()` guard before cleanup request) | AP64 (`route.fetch()` after context close) |
| Order-dependent failure not reproducible locally | Seed not captured from CI | Pattern 135 (`--randomly-seed` capture + GitHub step summary) | Gotcha 64 (`--randomly-seed=0` not fixed) |
| E2E suite flaky due to third-party analytics scripts | Real network calls to unstable CDNs | Pattern 130 (`page.route()` abort for analytics domains) | Allowing all third-party scripts in E2E |
| Background job test hangs for full timeout every run | No back-off polling — linear wait | Pattern 139 (`expect(fn).toPass({ intervals })` exponential back-off) | `waitForTimeout(15000)` hardcoded delay |
| `trace: 'on-first-retry'` generates no trace locally | `retries: 0` means condition never fires | Gotcha 65 (use `retain-on-failure` locally) | `on-first-retry` without checking retry count |

### New Patterns (Cycle 25)

---

### Pattern 140 — Vitest 4.1 `aroundAll` Hook for Database Transaction Rollback Across a Full Test Suite  [community]

Vitest 4.1 introduced `aroundAll` — a symmetric wrapper hook that encloses an entire `describe`
block's lifecycle. The primary production use case is database transaction isolation: start a
transaction in `aroundAll`, run all tests inside it, then roll back unconditionally after the
last test. This is strictly superior to `beforeAll`/`afterAll` pairs because the rollback is
guaranteed even if `afterAll` is never reached (e.g., process kill, uncaught exception).

```typescript
// tests/integration/order-service.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from 'vitest';
import { db } from '../../src/db';
import { OrderService } from '../../src/services/order-service';

describe('OrderService integration', async (suite) => {
  // aroundAll receives a `runSuite` callback — call it to execute the tests.
  // Everything before runSuite() is setup; everything after is teardown.
  // Guaranteed teardown even on signal/kill — no dangling transactions.
  suite.aroundAll(async (runSuite) => {
    const tx = await db.transaction();

    try {
      // Inject the transaction into all tests via AsyncLocalStorage or DI.
      // Here we use a module-level export that OrderService reads:
      process.env.TEST_TX_CLIENT = tx.id;
      await runSuite();
    } finally {
      // ALWAYS rolls back — even if runSuite() throws or is killed mid-run.
      await tx.rollback();
      delete process.env.TEST_TX_CLIENT;
    }
  });

  test('creates order and deducts inventory', async () => {
    const service = new OrderService({ txId: process.env.TEST_TX_CLIENT });
    const order = await service.createOrder({ productId: 'prod-1', quantity: 2 });
    expect(order.id).toMatch(/^ord-/);
    // Inventory deduction is rolled back after the suite — no fixture cleanup needed.
    const stock = await service.getStock('prod-1');
    expect(stock.available).toBe(98); // started at 100
  });

  test('rejects order when inventory is insufficient', async () => {
    const service = new OrderService({ txId: process.env.TEST_TX_CLIENT });
    await expect(
      service.createOrder({ productId: 'prod-1', quantity: 999 })
    ).rejects.toThrow('insufficient inventory');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff vs `beforeAll`/`afterAll`:** The `aroundAll` wrapper is slightly harder to reason about
for teams unfamiliar with it — the transaction begins before the first `beforeAll` hook and rolls
back after the last `afterAll`. This order matters: data seeded in a `beforeAll` hook is still
within the transaction. Document the scoping explicitly in a comment. The pattern does NOT work
with tests that spawn separate processes (worker pool `vmForks`) because the transaction is
process-local — keep integration tests in the `forks` pool with process-level DB teardown.

---

### Pattern 141 — Vitest 3.2 `using` Keyword for Automatic `vi.spyOn` Restoration  [community]

TypeScript 5.2+ explicit resource management (`using` keyword) allows any object with a
`[Symbol.dispose]` method to be automatically cleaned up when the enclosing block exits. Vitest
3.2 made `vi.spyOn()` return a disposable spy, so pairing `using` with spies eliminates the
`afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks())` boilerplate — and prevents the class of flakiness where
a developer forgets to restore a spy in a complex test with early returns.

```typescript
// tests/unit/notification.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
import { sendWelcomeEmail } from '../../src/notifications';
import * as mailer from '../../src/mailer';

describe('sendWelcomeEmail', () => {
  test('calls mailer.send with correct subject', () => {
    // `using` automatically calls spy.mockRestore() when this test block exits.
    // This works even if the test throws early — no dangling spy.
    using sendSpy = vi.spyOn(mailer, 'send').mockResolvedValue({ messageId: 'msg-1' });

    sendWelcomeEmail({ email: 'user@example.com', name: 'Alice' });

    expect(sendSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({
        to: 'user@example.com',
        subject: expect.stringContaining('Welcome'),
      })
    );
    // No afterEach needed — spy is restored as `using` block exits.
  });

  test('does NOT call mailer in dry-run mode', () => {
    // Previous test's spy is already restored here — isolation guaranteed.
    using sendSpy = vi.spyOn(mailer, 'send');

    sendWelcomeEmail({ email: 'user@example.com', name: 'Bob', dryRun: true });

    expect(sendSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});
```

**Critical caveat:** `using` only works for `vi.spyOn()` targets. Standalone `vi.fn()` mocks do
not have `[Symbol.dispose]` and are NOT auto-cleaned. Combine `using` for spies with
`resetMocks: true` in `vitest.config.ts` to cover both cases. The anti-pattern to avoid is
removing `restoreMocks: true` from config because "we now use `using`" — they cover different
mock types.

---

### Pattern 142 — Vitest 3.2 `scope: 'file'` Fixtures for Shared Test Infrastructure  [community]

Vitest 3.2 added `scope: 'file'` (and `scope: 'worker'`) to the `test.extend` fixture system.
A `file`-scoped fixture initializes once per test file and tears down after all tests in that
file complete — like a `beforeAll`/`afterAll` pair but lazy (only initializes if the fixture is
actually used). This is the correct pattern for expensive shared infrastructure like in-memory
databases, mock servers, and HTTP listeners.

```typescript
// fixtures/mock-server.ts
import { test as base } from 'vitest';
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node';
import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';

interface ServerFixtures {
  mockServer: ReturnType<typeof setupServer>;
}

// `scope: 'file'` — server starts once per file, not once per test.
// Without this, a new server starts/stops for every test case — slow and flaky
// (port binding race on rapid setup/teardown).
export const test = base.extend<ServerFixtures>({
  mockServer: [
    async (_, use) => {
      const server = setupServer(
        http.get('/api/products', () =>
          HttpResponse.json([{ id: 1, name: 'Widget' }])
        )
      );
      server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' });

      await use(server);

      // Teardown runs after ALL tests in this file complete.
      server.close();
    },
    { scope: 'file' }, // ← key: file-level lifetime, not test-level
  ],
});

// tests/components/product-list.test.ts
import { test } from '../fixtures/mock-server';
import { describe, expect } from 'vitest';

describe('ProductList', () => {
  test('renders products from API', async ({ mockServer }) => {
    // mockServer is the same instance across all tests in this file.
    // No port-binding race; no startup overhead per test.
    const res = await fetch('/api/products');
    const data = await res.json();
    expect(data).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test('shows empty state when no products', async ({ mockServer }) => {
    // Override the handler for this specific test only.
    mockServer.use(
      http.get('/api/products', () => HttpResponse.json([]))
    );
    const res = await fetch('/api/products');
    expect(await res.json()).toEqual([]);
    // MSW's `use()` overrides are per-request; previous handler restores after.
  });
});
```

**Community signal:** Before `scope: 'file'`, teams used a `beforeAll(() => server.listen()) /
afterAll(() => server.close())` pattern at the top of each test file — 20–30 lines of setup
per file. The `scope: 'file'` fixture centralizes this in one place and makes it opt-in per
test file, eliminating copy-paste drift where some files started with `onUnhandledRequest: 'warn'`
and others with `'error'`, causing inconsistent flakiness behavior.

---

### Pattern 143 — Playwright `testInfoError.errorContext` Aria Snapshot for DOM-State Flakiness Diagnosis  [community]

Playwright v1.60 introduced `testInfoError.errorContext` which surfaces additional diagnostic
information alongside matcher failures — specifically, the ARIA snapshot of the page or locator
at the time of the failure. This is invaluable for diagnosing "element not visible" flakiness
where the page state at failure time is unknown from logs alone.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — enable errorContext in HTML reporter
import { defineConfig, Reporter } from '@playwright/test';

// Custom reporter that extracts errorContext from each test's errors.
class AriaContextReporter implements Reporter {
  onTestEnd(test: any, result: any) {
    for (const error of result.errors) {
      if (error.errorContext) {
        // errorContext contains the ARIA tree of the receiver locator
        // at the exact moment the assertion failed.
        console.log(
          `[flakiness-context] Test: ${test.title}\n` +
          `  Aria snapshot at failure:\n${error.errorContext}`
        );
      }
    }
  }
}

export default defineConfig({
  reporter: [
    ['html', { open: 'never' }],
    ['./reporters/aria-context-reporter.ts'],
  ],
  retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,
});

// Example: a flaky test that fails with toBeVisible()
// tests/checkout.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('cart badge shows correct count', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/shop');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).first().click();

  // When this assertion fails due to a loading spinner covering the badge,
  // errorContext automatically includes the ARIA tree showing the spinner
  // is the topmost visible element — revealing the root cause.
  await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-badge')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-badge')).toContainText('1');
});
```

**Why this matters for flakiness triage:** Before `errorContext`, diagnosing "element not
visible" flakiness required reproductions with `--trace on` or screenshot captures in
`afterEach`. The ARIA snapshot surfaces the DOM state directly in CI log output without any
reproduction effort — often revealing within seconds that a loading spinner, cookie banner, or
skeleton placeholder was covering the target element at the moment of failure.

---

### Pattern 144 — Playwright `reporter.onError()` `workerInfo` for Parallel Fixture Teardown Failures  [community]

Playwright v1.60 extended the `reporter.onError()` callback to include a `workerInfo` argument
when the error originates from a fixture teardown in a parallel worker. Without this, fixture
teardown errors in workers appear as anonymous errors in the HTML report — no test name, no
file path, no way to know which test's fixture caused the problem. The `workerInfo` context
pinpoints the worker and its active test, enabling targeted investigation.

```typescript
// reporters/worker-error-reporter.ts
import { Reporter, TestError, WorkerInfo } from '@playwright/test/reporter';
import * as fs from 'fs';

export default class WorkerErrorReporter implements Reporter {
  private workerErrors: Array<{ worker: WorkerInfo; error: TestError }> = [];

  onError(error: TestError, workerInfo?: WorkerInfo): void {
    if (workerInfo) {
      // This error came from a worker fixture teardown, not from test body.
      // Log enough context to identify the root cause.
      this.workerErrors.push({ worker: workerInfo, error });
      console.error(
        `[worker-teardown-error] Worker ${workerInfo.workerIndex} ` +
        `(parallel index: ${workerInfo.parallelIndex})\n` +
        `  Error: ${error.message}\n` +
        `  This error occurred during fixture teardown — check fixtures ` +
        `used by tests on worker ${workerInfo.workerIndex}.`
      );
    }
  }

  onEnd(): void {
    if (this.workerErrors.length > 0) {
      // Write structured report for CI annotation.
      const report = this.workerErrors.map(({ worker, error }) => ({
        workerIndex: worker.workerIndex,
        parallelIndex: worker.parallelIndex,
        error: error.message,
        stack: error.stack,
      }));
      fs.writeFileSync(
        'worker-teardown-errors.json',
        JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)
      );
    }
  }
}
```

**Community signal:** Teams running 8+ parallel workers in CI encounter fixture teardown errors
that silently disappear in the HTML report's "Errors" section. The `workerInfo` field was added
specifically because the Playwright team observed in GitHub issues that teams spent hours trying
to reproduce a worker-specific teardown error that only manifested with more than 4 workers,
because the timing of the DB connection pool exhaustion was worker-count-dependent.

---

### Pattern 145 — Playwright Component Testing: Avoiding `vi.mock()` / `jest.mock()` at Module Level  [community]

Playwright component testing runs the test file in Node.js (where `vi.mock()` applies) but
the component bundle runs in the browser (where module-level mocks do NOT apply). Teams that
mock an API client with `vi.mock('../../src/api-client')` at the top of a CT spec discover
that the component continues to import the real API client at runtime — the mock only affects
the test harness, not the browser bundle.

```typescript
// ❌ BROKEN: module-level mock does NOT cross the browser bundle boundary
// tests/components/product-card.spec.tsx
import { vi, describe, test, expect } from 'vitest';
import { mount } from '@playwright/experimental-ct-react';
import { ProductCard } from '../../src/components/ProductCard';

// This mock runs in Node.js test process — NOT in the browser where the component runs.
vi.mock('../../src/api-client', () => ({
  fetchProduct: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ id: 1, name: 'Widget', price: 9.99 }),
}));

test('shows product name', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount(<ProductCard productId={1} />);
  // Component fetches from the REAL api-client in the browser — not the mock.
  // Test may pass or fail non-deterministically depending on network.
  await expect(component.getByText('Widget')).toBeVisible();
});

// ✅ CORRECT: pass test behavior through mount options → beforeMount hook
// playwright/index.tsx (browser-side setup file)
import { beforeMount } from '@playwright/experimental-ct-react/hooks';
import { type ApiClient } from '../src/api-client';

let mockApiClient: Partial<ApiClient> | null = null;

beforeMount(async ({ hooksConfig }: { hooksConfig?: { mockApi?: Partial<ApiClient> } }) => {
  if (hooksConfig?.mockApi) {
    mockApiClient = hooksConfig.mockApi;
  }
});

// In the component, inject via React context or prop:
// tests/components/product-card.spec.tsx (corrected)
test('shows product name with injected mock', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount(<ProductCard productId={1} />, {
    hooksConfig: {
      mockApi: {
        fetchProduct: async () => ({ id: 1, name: 'Widget', price: 9.99 }),
      },
    },
  });
  await expect(component.getByText('Widget')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(component.getByText('$9.99')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Why this is a flakiness source:** The broken pattern produces non-deterministic tests that pass
locally when the dev server is running (real API responds quickly) but fail in CI (no API server,
or slow response causes timeout). Teams spend time adding retries when the root fix is moving
the mock to the browser-side `beforeMount` hook. The Playwright docs state this explicitly but
the `vi.mock` habit from unit testing is deeply ingrained.

---

### Pattern 146 — Playwright `tracing.group()` / `groupEnd()` for Structured Trace Investigation  [community]

Playwright v1.49 added `tracing.group()` and `tracing.groupEnd()` to the Trace Viewer, allowing
test authors to create logical groupings of trace steps. In long E2E tests with many actions,
ungrouped traces become impossible to navigate — every `click`, `fill`, and `waitFor` appears
at the same depth. Grouping by user journey step makes flakiness identification immediate.

```typescript
// tests/e2e/checkout.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('complete purchase flow', async ({ page }) => {
  // Group 1: Browse and select product
  await test.step('Browse catalog and select product', async () => {
    await page.context().tracing.group('1. Browse catalog');
    await page.goto('/shop');
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Widgets' }).click();
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart', }).first().click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-count')).toContainText('1');
    await page.context().tracing.groupEnd();
  });

  // Group 2: Checkout form
  await test.step('Fill checkout form', async () => {
    await page.context().tracing.group('2. Checkout form');
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Cart' }).click();
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Proceed to checkout' }).click();
    await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('test@example.com');
    await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4111111111111111');
    await page.getByLabel('Expiry').fill('12/28');
    await page.getByLabel('CVV').fill('123');
    await page.context().tracing.groupEnd();
  });

  // Group 3: Submit and confirm
  await test.step('Submit order', async () => {
    await page.context().tracing.group('3. Order submission');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();
    // This assertion is flaky when the order confirmation takes >2s.
    // In the Trace Viewer, this step is in group "3. Order submission" —
    // immediately visible without scrolling through 80+ ungrouped steps.
    await expect(page.getByText('Order confirmed')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await page.context().tracing.groupEnd();
  });
});
```

**Why grouping matters for flakiness triage:** An E2E test with 50 steps generates a Trace
Viewer timeline with 50 entries at the same indentation level. Identifying which step group
contains the flaky action requires scrolling through all 50. With `tracing.group()`, the failing
step appears in a named group that collapses the preceding steps — reducing investigation time
from 10 minutes of scrolling to 30 seconds of click-to-expand.

---

### Pattern 147 — Vitest `sequence.groupOrder` for Deterministic Test Phase Ordering  [community]

Vitest 3.2 introduced `sequence.groupOrder` as a numeric priority for Vitest workspace projects.
Projects with the same `groupOrder` value run together (in parallel), and groups run from lowest
to highest. This enables a CI pipeline pattern where unit tests (fast, high confidence) must
complete before integration tests run — preventing slow, flaky integration suites from running
in parallel with fast unit suites where a shared test database becomes a contention point.

```typescript
// vitest.workspace.ts
import { defineWorkspace } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineWorkspace([
  // Group 0: unit tests — run first, fastest, no external deps.
  {
    test: {
      name: 'unit',
      include: ['src/**/*.unit.test.ts'],
      environment: 'node',
      sequence: {
        groupOrder: 0, // runs first
      },
    },
  },
  // Group 1: integration tests — run after unit tests complete.
  // Shares a test database that would be corrupted by parallel unit test mocks.
  {
    test: {
      name: 'integration',
      include: ['src/**/*.integration.test.ts'],
      environment: 'node',
      globalSetup: ['./setup/db-integration.ts'],
      sequence: {
        groupOrder: 1, // runs after all groupOrder 0 projects finish
      },
    },
  },
  // Group 2: browser tests — run last, most expensive.
  {
    test: {
      name: 'browser',
      include: ['src/**/*.browser.test.ts'],
      browser: { enabled: true, name: 'chromium', provider: 'playwright' },
      sequence: {
        groupOrder: 2, // runs after integration tests complete
      },
    },
  },
]);
```

**Tradeoff vs simple `--project` flags:** `groupOrder` is declarative — it lives in the config
and is version-controlled. Manually ordering `vitest --project unit && vitest --project integration`
in CI scripts duplicates the sequencing logic in every CI YAML file that runs tests, creating
drift when a new project is added. The workspace `groupOrder` approach means adding a new test
project in the config automatically participates in the correct execution phase.

---

### Pattern 148 — Playwright `--last-failed` Fast Triage Loop for CI Flakiness Investigation  [community]

When a CI run produces 3–5 flaky test failures across a 500-test suite, re-running the entire
suite to reproduce them locally wastes 20–30 minutes. Playwright's `--last-failed` CLI option
(v1.44+) reads the last JSON report and runs ONLY the tests that failed, enabling a tight
reproduce-fix-verify loop without waiting for the full suite.

```typescript
// package.json scripts
// "test:e2e": "playwright test",
// "test:e2e:retry-failed": "playwright test --last-failed",
// "test:e2e:ci": "playwright test --reporter=json,html"

// playwright.config.ts — ensure JSON reporter always runs so --last-failed has data
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
export default defineConfig({
  reporter: process.env.CI
    ? [['json', { outputFile: 'test-results/results.json' }], ['html', { open: 'never' }]]
    : [['json', { outputFile: 'test-results/results.json' }], ['list']],
  retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,
  use: {
    trace: 'retain-on-failure',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
  },
});

// CI step: annotate PR with triage command when tests fail
// .github/workflows/e2e.yml (partial)
// - name: Annotate with reproduction command
//   if: failure()
//   run: |
//     echo "### Reproduce failing E2E tests" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
//     echo "\`\`\`bash" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
//     echo "# Download test-results/results.json from CI artifacts, then:" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
//     echo "npx playwright test --last-failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
//     echo "\`\`\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
```

**Community signal:** Teams that document `--last-failed` in their onboarding materials report
that new engineers reproduce flaky test failures 5× faster than those who re-run the full suite.
The critical requirement: the JSON reporter must run in EVERY CI job (not just on failure), and
the `test-results/results.json` artifact must be downloadable. Teams that only save artifacts
on failure lose the baseline needed for `--last-failed` to know what passed.

---

### Pattern 149 — Vitest `getSeed()` + Global Setup for Reproducible Suite Shuffling  [community]

Vitest's `getSeed()` function returns the random seed used for the current test run's shuffled
order. Capturing this in a `globalSetup` file and writing it to a CI artifact allows perfect
reproduction of any order-dependent failure. The critical rule: `getSeed()` must be called in
`globalSetup` or `setupFiles`, NOT inside test bodies — it returns `undefined` when called
inside a test function.

```typescript
// vitest.setup-global.ts (runs once per Vitest process)
import { getSeed } from 'vitest';

export async function setup() {
  const seed = getSeed();
  console.log(`[vitest] Shuffling seed: ${seed}`);

  // Write seed to file so CI can upload it as an artifact and include in step summary.
  const { writeFileSync } = await import('fs');
  writeFileSync('vitest-seed.txt', String(seed), 'utf8');

  // Expose for use in other setup scripts via environment variable.
  process.env.VITEST_SEED = String(seed);
}

// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    // Shuffle test execution order for order-dependency detection.
    sequence: {
      shuffle: true,
      // Optionally fix the seed for a deterministic run (e.g., during bisection):
      // seed: 12345,
    },
    globalSetup: ['./vitest.setup-global.ts'],
  },
});

// .github/workflows/unit.yml (partial)
// - name: Upload Vitest seed
//   if: failure()
//   uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
//   with:
//     name: vitest-seed
//     path: vitest-seed.txt
//     retention-days: 7
// - name: Annotate PR with reproduction command
//   if: failure()
//   run: |
//     SEED=$(cat vitest-seed.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
//     echo "Reproduce: \`npx vitest run --sequence.seed=$SEED\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
```

**Anti-pattern:** Calling `getSeed()` inside a `test()` body to log it. This returns `undefined`
because the seed is resolved during the test runner's initialization phase, before individual
test functions are called. The function is designed for `globalSetup` and `setupFiles` context
only.

---

### Pattern 150 — Vitest `fakeTimers` with `shouldClearNativeTimers: true` for Full Timer Isolation  [community]

A subtle class of flakiness occurs when `vi.useFakeTimers()` is called but the default
`shouldClearNativeTimers: false` leaves any timers created before the fake-timer install
(e.g., timers from module initialization) as real timers. These real timers fire during the
test, executing callbacks against the fake-timer environment — causing non-deterministic
behavior that only reproduces with specific module loading order.

```typescript
// tests/unit/polling-service.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { PollingService } from '../../src/polling-service';

describe('PollingService timer isolation', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    // shouldClearNativeTimers: true cancels all real timers created before install().
    // This includes module-level setInterval() calls from imported singletons.
    // Without this, those real timers fire at wall-clock time DURING the fake-timer test,
    // corrupting the fake timeline (e.g., a real 100ms timer fires at fake-timer step 50ms,
    // triggering a callback that expects the fake clock to be at 100ms).
    vi.useFakeTimers({
      shouldClearNativeTimers: true,
      // Advance timers automatically on every awaited Promise to avoid deadlocks.
      toFake: ['setTimeout', 'setInterval', 'Date', 'performance'],
    });
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    vi.useRealTimers();
  });

  test('polls exactly 3 times within 300ms window', async () => {
    const mockFetch = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ status: 'pending' });
    const service = new PollingService(mockFetch, { intervalMs: 100 });

    service.start();

    // Advance fake clock by 300ms — triggers 3 poll intervals.
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300);

    expect(mockFetch).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
    service.stop();
  });

  test('stops polling after max attempts', async () => {
    const mockFetch = vi.fn()
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ status: 'pending' })
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ status: 'pending' })
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ status: 'completed' }); // stops here

    const service = new PollingService(mockFetch, { intervalMs: 100, maxAttempts: 5 });
    service.start();

    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(500);

    // Should stop after 3 attempts (status=completed), not continue to 5.
    expect(mockFetch).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
  });
});
```

**Community signal:** The `shouldClearNativeTimers` option is documented but rarely used in
examples. Teams hitting the "real timer interferes with fake timer" pattern typically spend
2–3 hours narrowing down which import creates the interfering timer before finding this option.
Add `shouldClearNativeTimers: true` to every `vi.useFakeTimers()` call in a team coding standard
document to prevent the class entirely.

---

### Pattern 151 — Playwright `page.addLocatorHandler()` `times` Option for Bounded Overlay Dismissal  [community]

`page.addLocatorHandler()` registers a callback that fires whenever an overlay blocks an
actionability check. Without the `times` option, the handler fires indefinitely for the lifetime
of the page — even in phases of the test where the overlay should not appear. A handler firing
unexpectedly in a later test phase (e.g., during a form submission) can introduce unintended
clicks that corrupt test state. The `times` option limits handler invocations to a bounded count.

```typescript
// tests/e2e/onboarding.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('new user completes onboarding without cookie banner interference', async ({ page }) => {
  // Register a bounded handler: fires at MOST once, then auto-removes.
  // Without `times: 1`, this handler fires every time ANY locator check sees the banner —
  // including during form submission, which could click "Dismiss" mid-POST request.
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Cookie preferences' }),
    async (dialog) => {
      await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: 'Accept all' }).click();
    },
    { times: 1 } // dismiss once only; remove handler after first invocation
  );

  await page.goto('/onboarding');

  // Step 1: Profile setup — cookie banner may appear here.
  await page.getByLabel('Full name').fill('Alice Smith');
  await page.getByLabel('Job title').fill('Engineer');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue' }).click();

  // Step 2: Preferences — handler is already consumed; no spurious dismissal here.
  await expect(page.getByText('Step 2: Preferences')).toBeVisible();
  await page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Email updates' }).check();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Finish setup' }).click();

  await expect(page.getByText('Setup complete')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Setting `times: 1` assumes the overlay appears exactly once per test. If the
cookie banner reappears after navigation (SPA that re-triggers consent on every route change),
use `times: N` or omit the `times` option and ensure the handler is cheap (just a `click`,
no `waitForResponse`). Always log handler invocations (`console.log` inside the handler) during
initial setup to verify the count assumption before removing logging.

---

### Anti-Patterns (Cycle 25)

#### AP66 — Using `aroundAll` Without Calling `runSuite()` in the Happy Path  [community]
**What:** Implementing an `aroundAll` hook that calls `runSuite()` inside a `try` block but
not calling it at all in some code paths (e.g., an early return when a setup precondition fails).
**Why harmful:** If `runSuite()` is never called, all tests in the suite are silently skipped —
they appear as never executed in the report, not as failures. This can mask entire test suites
failing silently in CI if a setup check fails. Always call `runSuite()` unconditionally; use
`test.skip()` inside tests for conditional skipping, and throw from `aroundAll` setup if
infrastructure is unavailable.

#### AP67 — Removing `restoreMocks: true` from Config Because `using` Handles Spy Cleanup  [community]
**What:** After adopting the `using vi.spyOn(...)` pattern (Pattern 141), removing `restoreMocks:
true` from `vitest.config.ts` because "we now have auto-cleanup."
**Why harmful:** `using` only handles `vi.spyOn()` disposables. Standalone `vi.fn()` mocks —
created directly without `spyOn` — do not implement `[Symbol.dispose]` and are NOT auto-restored.
A codebase with both `vi.fn()` and `vi.spyOn()` will have inconsistent cleanup. Keep
`restoreMocks: true` in config as the global safety net regardless of whether `using` is adopted.

#### AP68 — Using `scope: 'file'` Fixtures in a Suite With `fileParallelism: true`  [community]
**What:** Defining a `scope: 'file'` fixture (e.g., a shared MSW server) while also enabling
`fileParallelism: true` in the Vitest config — which runs multiple files concurrently in the
same worker.
**Why harmful:** `scope: 'file'` fixtures are designed with the assumption that only one file
runs per worker at a time. With `fileParallelism: true`, multiple files share a worker, and
multiple `scope: 'file'` fixture instances race to bind to the same port or access the same
resource. This causes `EADDRINUSE` errors or corrupted state. Either disable `fileParallelism`
for suites using `scope: 'file'` fixtures, or use `scope: 'worker'` and accept that the
fixture lives longer than a single file.

---

### Real-World Gotchas (Cycle 25)  [community]

**Gotcha 66 — Vitest 4.1 `FixtureAccessError` When Accessing `test`-Scoped Fixtures in `beforeAll`**  [community]
Vitest 4.1 introduced an explicit `FixtureAccessError` thrown when a `test`-scoped fixture is
accessed inside `beforeAll` or `afterAll` hooks. In previous Vitest versions, this silently
returned `undefined` — leading to subtle flakiness where the fixture value was used but
happened to be `undefined` for non-obvious reasons. The new explicit error is a strict
improvement, but it breaks existing test suites that accidentally relied on the silent `undefined`
behavior. Fix: move `test`-scoped fixture setup into `beforeEach`, or change the fixture
`scope` to `'file'` if the intent is to share across the suite.

**Gotcha 67 — Playwright `context.route()` vs `page.route()` Registration Order Race**  [community]
When both `context.route()` and `page.route()` intercept the same URL pattern, Playwright
evaluates handlers in LIFO order (last registered wins). Teams that register a `context.route()`
baseline interceptor in a fixture and then add a `page.route()` override in a specific test
find that the behavior is correct as long as the `page.route()` is registered AFTER the
`context.route()`. If the context handler is registered lazily (e.g., inside an `async () =>`
that resolves after page navigation starts), the context handler may register AFTER the page
handler — reversing the override priority and causing flakiness that only manifests on slow CI
runners where async fixture setup takes longer.

**Gotcha 68 — Vitest `using vi.spyOn()` in a `describe` Block Outside `test()` Creates a Shared Spy**  [community]
The `using` keyword auto-restores the spy when the enclosing block exits. If `using spy = vi.spyOn(...)`
is placed at `describe` block level (outside any `test()`), the `using` block is the `describe`
callback scope — which exits before any test runs. The spy is restored immediately, before the
tests execute, making it a no-op for all test cases in the block. `using` for spies must be
placed inside `test()` or `beforeEach()` callbacks to work correctly.

**Gotcha 69 — Playwright `tracing.group()` Leaks When Test Throws Before `groupEnd()`**  [community]
If a test throws between `tracing.group()` and `tracing.groupEnd()`, the trace group is never
closed. In the Trace Viewer, all subsequent steps from other tests are nested inside the
unclosed group, making the trace unreadable for every test that follows in the same worker.
Fix: wrap the group body in a `try/finally`:
```typescript
await page.context().tracing.group('3. Order submission');
try {
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByText('Order confirmed')).toBeVisible();
} finally {
  await page.context().tracing.groupEnd(); // always closes the group
}
```
Alternatively, use Playwright's `test.step()` API which handles this automatically via its
built-in scoping — `tracing.group()` is a lower-level alternative for cases where the step
metadata model is insufficient.

**Gotcha 70 — Vitest `sequence.groupOrder` Does Not Prevent Files Within a Group from Running in Parallel**  [community]
Teams using `groupOrder` to sequence unit → integration → browser testing sometimes expect that
`groupOrder: 1` integration tests run serially (one by one) after unit tests complete. This is
not the case: `groupOrder` sequences project groups, not individual test files. Within a group,
all test files still run in parallel according to the pool configuration. If true serialization
of individual integration test files is needed (e.g., each file resets the same DB table),
combine `groupOrder` with `pool: 'forks'` and `maxForks: 1` for the integration project, or
use `sequence.concurrent: false` for that specific project.

---

### Quick Reference additions (Cycle 25)

| Symptom | Likely Root Cause | Pattern/Fix | Anti-Pattern to Avoid |
|---------|-------------------|-------------|----------------------|
| DB integration tests corrupt each other's state | No transaction rollback boundary | Pattern 140 (`aroundAll` DB transaction rollback) | AP66 (`aroundAll` without calling `runSuite()`) |
| `vi.spyOn` persists to next test despite `using` keyword | `vi.fn()` mocks not covered by `using` | Pattern 141 + keep `restoreMocks: true` in config | AP67 (removing `restoreMocks: true` after adopting `using`) |
| MSW server port collision on rapid test teardown | `beforeAll`/`afterAll` server start/stop per test | Pattern 142 (`scope: 'file'` fixture for shared server) | AP68 (`scope: 'file'` + `fileParallelism: true`) |
| "Element not visible" failure — unknown DOM state at failure time | No DOM snapshot at failure | Pattern 143 (`testInfoError.errorContext` ARIA snapshot reporter) | No errorContext extraction in reporter |
| Parallel worker fixture teardown errors appear anonymously | No `workerInfo` extraction from `reporter.onError()` | Pattern 144 (`workerInfo` structured teardown error report) | No worker context in error logging |
| CT component fetches real API — mock not applied | `vi.mock()` boundary does not cross into browser | Pattern 145 (pass mock via `hooksConfig` in `mount()`) | Module-level `vi.mock()` in component tests |
| Long E2E trace unreadable — all steps flat | No logical grouping in trace | Pattern 146 (`tracing.group()` / `groupEnd()` per user journey step) | Gotcha 69 (group not closed on exception) |
| Unit and integration tests share a DB and interfere | Both run in parallel in same Vitest run | Pattern 147 (`sequence.groupOrder` to phase unit → integration) | Gotcha 70 (expecting `groupOrder` to serialize files within group) |
| `--last-failed` has no data to work from | JSON reporter not enabled or artifact not saved | Pattern 148 (JSON reporter in every CI job + artifact upload) | JSON reporter only on failure |
| Order-dependent failure not reproducible locally | Seed not captured | Pattern 149 (`getSeed()` in `globalSetup` + seed artifact) | AP in Pattern 149 (`getSeed()` inside test body returns `undefined`) |
| Real timer fires during fake-timer test — non-deterministic | Module-level setInterval not cleared | Pattern 150 (`shouldClearNativeTimers: true` in `useFakeTimers`) | `vi.useFakeTimers()` without `shouldClearNativeTimers` |
| Cookie banner handler fires during form submission — corrupts state | Unbounded `addLocatorHandler` without `times` | Pattern 151 (`times: 1` on bounded overlay handler) | AP61 (navigation handler without post-handler URL accounting) |
| All tests in `aroundAll` suite silently skipped | `runSuite()` never called in setup failure path | AP66 (always call `runSuite()` unconditionally) | Early return from `aroundAll` without calling `runSuite()` |
| Vitest `beforeAll` fixture access throws `FixtureAccessError` | `test`-scoped fixture accessed in `beforeAll` (Vitest 4.1) | Gotcha 66 (move to `beforeEach` or change fixture scope) | Relying on old silent `undefined` behavior |
| `context.route()` handler takes priority unexpectedly over `page.route()` | Lazy async context handler registers after page handler (LIFO) | Gotcha 67 (ensure `context.route()` registered eagerly before `page.route()`) | Async fixture setup registering context routes after test begins |
