## Cycle 26 — 2026-05-13

### Pattern 152 — Vitest `retry.condition` Regex for Selective Network-Error Retries  [official]

Retrying on every failure masks real regressions. Vitest's `retry.condition` option (v4.1+)
accepts a regex matched against the error message, enabling tests to retry ONLY on transient
network-related errors while letting assertion failures fail fast. This prevents the failure
classification distortion that occurs when broad retries absorb genuine defects.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    // Retry up to 2 times, but ONLY for transient network errors.
    // Assertion failures (expect(x).toBe(y)) do NOT match this pattern
    // and fail immediately on first attempt — no retry tax on fast paths.
    retry: {
      count: 2,
      delay: 500,
      condition: /ECONNRESET|ETIMEDOUT|ECONNREFUSED|fetch failed|network error/i,
    },
    // Use slowTestThreshold to surface tests that are slow only when retried.
    slowTestThreshold: 2000,
  },
});
```

**When to use:** Integration tests that hit real Docker-hosted services (Postgres, Redis, S3-mock)
where connection resets happen on container warm-up. The regex ensures a failed `expect(user.id).toBe(42)`
is never silently retried — only socket-level errors qualify.

**When NOT to use:** Unit tests with fake timers or mocked modules — those have no network
surface area, and adding `retry.condition` there only adds misleading log noise.

**Named alternative:** `test.retry()` per-test override for surgically scoping retries without
touching the global config. Prefer the global `retry.condition` for consistency across the
project; use per-test override only for known-flaky third-party SDK calls.

[official] Vitest v4.1.6 CLI docs confirm `--retry.condition` accepts a regex pattern matched
against the error message, not the stack trace — match against human-readable error messages,
not internal module paths.

### Pattern 153 — Playwright `test.slow()` Adaptive Timeout for Environment-Dependent Tests  [official]

`test.slow()` multiplies the test's timeout by 3× without coupling the test to a hard numeric
value. When the base timeout changes in `playwright.config.ts`, all `slow` tests automatically
scale. This is safer than littering `test.setTimeout(90_000)` calls across the suite, which
drift from the base config over time and silently permit tests to run far longer than intended.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('pdf export generates and downloads in background', async ({ page }) => {
  // Signal this test inherently needs more time — 3x the base timeout.
  // If playwright.config.ts sets timeout: 30_000, this test gets 90_000.
  // When base is tuned down to 20_000 for perf, this test auto-scales to 60_000.
  test.slow();

  await page.goto('/reports/annual');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export PDF' }).click();

  // PDF generation is async; wait for download event rather than polling.
  const [download] = await Promise.all([
    page.waitForEvent('download'),
    page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Generate' }).click(),
  ]);

  expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toMatch(/annual-report.*\.pdf$/);
  await download.saveAs(`./test-results/${download.suggestedFilename()}`);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `test.slow()` does not communicate WHY a test is slow to reviewers. Pair it with
a comment explaining the inherent latency source (external process, large dataset, background
worker). Without the comment, future engineers remove `test.slow()` thinking it was added in
error — causing intermittent timeouts on slow CI runners.

[official] Playwright docs confirm `test.slow()` applies a 3x multiplier to both the test timeout
AND the expect assertion timeout for the duration of that test.

---

### Pattern 154 — Playwright `expect.poll()` for Polling External State Without `waitFor` Loops  [official]

Manual polling loops (`while (!(await checkCondition())) { await page.waitForTimeout(200); }`)
have three failure modes: they can loop forever if the timeout is not tracked separately; they
suppress intermediate errors; and they produce opaque failure messages. `expect.poll()` wraps
the same behavior in Playwright's assertion engine with auto-retrying, proper timeout, and
diff-quality failure messages.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { getJobStatus } from '../helpers/job-status-api';

test('background job transitions to completed state', async ({ request }) => {
  // Submit a long-running job via API.
  const response = await request.post('/api/jobs', {
    data: { type: 'dataExport', format: 'csv' },
  });
  const { jobId } = await response.json();

  // Poll external API until status is 'completed'. Playwright retries every
  // 500ms (default) up to the configured expect timeout (default 5s).
  // On failure, the diff shows actual vs expected value — no console.log needed.
  await expect.poll(
    () => getJobStatus(jobId),
    {
      message: `Job ${jobId} did not reach 'completed' within timeout`,
      intervals: [500, 1000, 2000, 5000], // Fibonacci-ish backoff
      timeout: 30_000,                     // Override expect timeout for slow jobs
    }
  ).toBe('completed');
});
```

**When to use:** Any test asserting on eventually-consistent external state: job queues, email
delivery checks, cache invalidation, webhook delivery confirmation.

**When NOT to use:** Do NOT use `expect.poll()` to work around a missing `await` on an async
locator action. If `expect(locator).toBeVisible()` is flaky, the fix is a proper locator, not
wrapping the check in `expect.poll()`.

[community] Teams that replaced while-loop polling with `expect.poll()` report that the interval
backoff option eliminates burst retries against a saturated job queue — reducing flakiness on
CI runners that share the job DB with other test workers.

---

### Pattern 155 — Vitest `repeats` + `retry` Dual Stability Confirmation Protocol  [official]

`repeats` and `retry` serve opposite purposes: `repeats` runs a passing test N more times to
confirm it never fails; `retry` re-runs a failing test to confirm it eventually passes. Using
both together creates a demanding stability gate for tests that touch shared infrastructure.
A test that `repeats: 4` and passes all 5 runs is far less likely to be a flaky false-positive
than one that passes once.

```typescript
import { it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { createTemporaryBucket } from '../helpers/storage';

// Stability gate for storage operations that touch shared S3-mock.
// The test must pass all 5 runs (1 original + 4 repeats).
// If any run fails, retry up to 2 times before marking as failed.
// Use during a "flakiness audit" sprint — remove before merging to main.
it('bucket creation is idempotent across concurrent requests',
  { repeats: 4, retry: 2 },
  async () => {
    const bucketName = `test-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
    const [result1, result2] = await Promise.all([
      createTemporaryBucket(bucketName),
      createTemporaryBucket(bucketName),
    ]);
    // Both calls should succeed without EEXIST error.
    expect(result1.status).toBe('created');
    expect(result2.status).toBe('created');
    // Cleanup.
    await result1.cleanup();
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff:** `repeats: 4` x `retry: 2` can execute a single test up to 15 times in worst case.
Never merge tests with `repeats > 0` to main — they inflate CI time multiplicatively. Tag them
with `{ tags: ['flaky-audit'] }` and strip `repeats` after the audit confirms stability.

[official] Vitest docs note that `repeats` is designed for debugging intermittent failures,
not for production test suites. The `getSeed()` + `repeats` combination (Pattern 149 + 155)
is the recommended workflow for order-dependent flakiness investigation.

---

### Pattern 156 — Playwright `testInfo.retry` Early-Exit for Expensive Teardown on Retry  [official]

Retried tests re-execute their full `beforeEach` and test body. If the test teardown involves
expensive operations (DB reset, file system cleanup, large API DELETE calls), running them on
every retry doubles or triples CI cost. `testInfo.retry` exposes the current retry count,
enabling conditional skip of expensive cleanup on intermediate retries where the test will run
again anyway.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.beforeEach(async ({ page, request }) => {
  // Always seed test data — needed for every attempt.
  await request.post('/api/test-setup', { data: { scenario: 'checkout-flow' } });
  await page.goto('/checkout');
});

test.afterEach(async ({ request }, testInfo) => {
  // Skip expensive DB purge on intermediate retries — the next retry's
  // beforeEach will re-seed anyway, and the purge adds 2s per retry cycle.
  if (testInfo.retry < testInfo.project.retries) {
    // Not the final attempt: skip full cleanup to save CI time.
    await request.delete('/api/test-cleanup/partial'); // lightweight reset only
    return;
  }
  // Final attempt (pass or last failure): run the full cleanup.
  await request.delete('/api/test-cleanup/full');
});

test('checkout flow completes with 3DS authentication', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay now' }).click();
  await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4000 0000 0000 3220');
  await expect(page.getByText('Authentication required')).toBeVisible();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Authenticate' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByText('Order confirmed')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**When to use:** Tests with per-test DB snapshots, test-scoped S3 prefixes, or browser
extension installs where teardown takes more than 1s.

**When NOT to use:** If your teardown ensures test isolation (e.g., rolling back a DB
transaction), skipping it on retry means the next attempt runs on dirty state — which can
CREATE flakiness rather than reduce it. Only skip cleanup that is genuinely idempotent on
re-entry.

[official] Playwright docs show `testInfo.retry` is 0-indexed: 0 = first attempt, 1 = first
retry. `testInfo.project.retries` is the max retries configured. Compare with `<` (not `<=`)
to identify non-final attempts.

---

### Pattern 157 — Vitest `mockImplementationOnce` Sequence for Multi-Call Flakiness Simulation  [community]

Flakiness from intermittent API failures is hard to test deterministically because it requires
the mock to fail on attempt N but succeed on attempt N+1. Using a sequence of
`mockImplementationOnce` calls simulates retry-aware behavior without stochastic logic — each
call in the mock returns a pre-defined response in order, matching what a real retry loop
experiences.

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
import { fetchUserProfile } from '../api/user';
import { fetchWithRetry } from '../utils/fetch-with-retry';

vi.mock('../api/user');
const mockFetch = vi.mocked(fetchUserProfile);

describe('fetchWithRetry under transient failures', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    mockFetch.mockReset();
  });

  it('retries on ECONNRESET and succeeds on third attempt', async () => {
    // Simulate: fail -> fail -> succeed (exactly 3 calls expected)
    mockFetch
      .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('ECONNRESET'))
      .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('ECONNRESET'))
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ id: 42, name: 'Alice' });

    const result = await fetchWithRetry(fetchUserProfile, { maxRetries: 3 });
    expect(result).toEqual({ id: 42, name: 'Alice' });
    expect(mockFetch).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
  });

  it('exhausts retries and throws after max attempts', async () => {
    mockFetch.mockRejectedValue(new Error('ECONNRESET')); // always fails
    await expect(fetchWithRetry(fetchUserProfile, { maxRetries: 2 }))
      .rejects.toThrow('ECONNRESET');
    expect(mockFetch).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3); // initial + 2 retries
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mockImplementationOnce` sequences are brittle to call-order changes. If the
implementation is refactored to call `fetchUserProfile` more times (e.g., for a pre-check),
the sequence silently shifts and the test asserts on wrong behavior. Use
`expect(mockFetch).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(N)` as a mandatory guard.

[community] A common gotcha: forgetting `mockReset()` in `beforeEach` after a sequence-based
test. The `mockImplementationOnce` queue carries over to the next test — the second test's
first call unexpectedly consumes the leftover "always fails" default from the previous test's
`mockRejectedValue()`.

---

### Pattern 158 — Playwright `page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` Anti-Pattern and Safe Alternative  [community]

`waitForLoadState('networkidle')` waits until there are no ongoing network requests for 500ms.
This is one of the most common sources of flakiness: analytics beacons, telemetry pings, and
polling APIs mean `networkidle` never fires in applications with long-running background requests.
Tests using it reliably on dev but failing on staging with telemetry enabled are a classic
signature of this root cause.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// FRAGILE: waitForLoadState('networkidle') fails when analytics or
// background polling is active in the environment.
// test('FRAGILE search results load', async ({ page }) => {
//   await page.goto('/search?q=laptop');
//   await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle'); // FLAKY if telemetry is on
//   expect(await page.locator('.product-card').count()).toBeGreaterThan(0);
// });

// STABLE: Assert on the actual UI state you care about.
// Playwright's web-first assertions auto-retry until the condition is met.
test('search results load and display product cards', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search?q=laptop');

  // Wait for the first result to appear — this is the real readiness signal.
  // Playwright retries the locator assertion until visible or timeout.
  const firstCard = page.getByTestId('product-card').first();
  await expect(firstCard).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 });

  // Now safe to count — DOM is in the state we care about.
  const cardCount = await page.getByTestId('product-card').count();
  expect(cardCount).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```

**When `networkidle` IS safe:** Static marketing pages, server-rendered apps with no client-side
polling, or tests explicitly running behind a request interceptor that blocks all background
traffic. In those narrow cases, `networkidle` is a valid readiness signal.

[community] Teams that audited their flaky E2E tests found `waitForLoadState('networkidle')`
present in 60-70% of their flaky tests. Replacing it with specific `expect(locator).toBeVisible()`
assertions reduced their flakiness rate from 8% to under 1% in a single sprint.

---

### Pattern 159 — Vitest `slowTestThreshold` + `onTestSlowness` Hook for Flakiness Pre-Detection  [official]

Tests that are slow on CI but fast locally are pre-flaky: they are one system-load spike away
from a timeout. Using `slowTestThreshold` to surface these tests, combined with a `onTestSlowness`
reporter hook, creates a proactive flakiness pipeline that flags slow tests BEFORE they cause
failures — not after.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — custom reporter for slow test CI annotations
import { defineConfig, type Reporter } from 'vitest/config';

const SLOW_THRESHOLD_MS = 300;

const slowTestAnnotator: Reporter = {
  onTestSlowness({ result, test }) {
    const ms = result.duration ?? 0;
    if (process.env.GITHUB_ACTIONS) {
      // Emit a GitHub Actions warning annotation visible inline in the PR check.
      const location = test.file?.name ?? 'unknown';
      process.stdout.write(
        `::warning file=${location},title=Slow test (${ms}ms)::` +
        `"${test.name}" ran for ${ms}ms — above ${SLOW_THRESHOLD_MS}ms threshold. ` +
        `Review for potential timeout flakiness.\n`
      );
    }
  },
};

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    slowTestThreshold: SLOW_THRESHOLD_MS,
    reporters: process.env.CI
      ? ['default', slowTestAnnotator]
      : ['default'],
  },
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `onTestSlowness` fires on every run including developer laptops with background
processes. Gating the GitHub Actions annotation behind `process.env.GITHUB_ACTIONS` prevents
noise during local runs. On CI, annotations appear inline in the PR check view — reviewers
see slow tests without reading the full log.

[official] Vitest v4.1.6 CLI docs confirm `--slowTestThreshold` accepts milliseconds and
defaults to 300ms. Tests exceeding the threshold are marked "SLOW" in the output and trigger
`onTestSlowness` in reporters.

---

### Pattern 160 — Playwright `context.storageState()` Lazy Snapshot vs Eager Snapshot for Auth Flakiness  [community]

The recommended Playwright auth pattern snapshots `storageState` after login and reuses it across
tests. A subtle flakiness source: if the snapshot is taken TOO EARLY (before the server-side
session is fully established), the snapshot captures an incomplete auth token. Tests that run
immediately after the snapshot see a 401 or partial-auth state — but only on slow CI where the
session propagation delay matters.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — auth setup project
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
export default defineConfig({
  projects: [
    {
      name: 'setup',
      testMatch: /global\.setup\.ts/,
    },
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      use: {
        storageState: 'playwright/.auth/user.json',
      },
      dependencies: ['setup'],
    },
  ],
});

// global.setup.ts — lazy snapshot with explicit readiness assertion
import { test as setup } from '@playwright/test';

setup('authenticate and snapshot storage state', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(process.env.TEST_USER_EMAIL!);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.TEST_USER_PASSWORD!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();

  // CRITICAL: Wait for a post-login element that only appears after the server
  // has fully established the session — NOT just after navigation completes.
  // Using waitForURL('/dashboard') alone is insufficient on slow auth services
  // because the redirect can complete before the session cookie is set.
  await expect(page.getByTestId('user-avatar')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15_000 });

  // NOW snapshot — session is fully established server-side.
  await page.context().storageState({ path: 'playwright/.auth/user.json' });
});
```

**When to use:** Any app where the auth token is issued asynchronously (OAuth, SAML, JWT
refresh). Wait for a UI element that is only rendered after the auth handshake completes —
not just after the URL changes.

[community] Auth setup flakiness is underreported because `setup` project failures often surface
as cryptic "depends on 'setup'" errors in dependent tests, not as obvious auth failures. If your
dependent tests show intermittent 401 responses, audit the snapshot timing in your setup project
first.

---

### Pattern 161 — Vitest `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: [...] })` Targeted Timer Replacement  [community]

`vi.useFakeTimers()` with no arguments replaces ALL timer APIs including `Date`, `setTimeout`,
`setInterval`, `queueMicrotask`, and `performance`. Third-party libraries that rely on real
`performance.now()` for internal bookkeeping (e.g., some logging libraries, OpenTelemetry SDK)
break silently when `performance` is faked — causing flaky failures that only appear when the
library happens to measure elapsed time during a test. The `toFake` option restricts replacement
to only the timers the test actually needs.

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect, vi, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { scheduleReminder } from '../services/reminder';

describe('reminder scheduling with controlled time', () => {
  afterEach(() => {
    vi.useRealTimers();
  });

  it('fires reminder after configured delay', async () => {
    // Only fake setTimeout and Date — do NOT fake performance or
    // queueMicrotask, which are used by the OpenTelemetry SDK in scope.
    vi.useFakeTimers({
      toFake: ['setTimeout', 'clearTimeout', 'Date'],
      now: new Date('2026-01-15T09:00:00Z'), // fixed reference point
    });

    const callback = vi.fn();
    scheduleReminder({ delayMs: 60_000, onFire: callback });

    // No callback yet — 60s has not elapsed.
    expect(callback).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

    // Advance fake timers by exactly 60 seconds.
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(60_000);

    expect(callback).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    expect(callback).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ firedAt: new Date('2026-01-15T09:01:00Z') })
    );
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Targeting only `['setTimeout', 'Date']` requires knowing which timer APIs your
code under test uses. If a future refactor introduces `setInterval`, the test silently stops
controlling it. Add a comment listing WHY each timer type is included/excluded so reviewers
understand the scope.

[community] The `shouldClearNativeTimers` option (Pattern 150) and `toFake` are complementary:
`shouldClearNativeTimers` clears EXISTING real timers before faking; `toFake` controls WHICH
APIs are replaced going forward. Both are needed to prevent module-level timers from leaking
into fake-timer tests.

---

### Pattern 162 — Playwright Locator `.and()` for Scoped Disambiguation Avoiding Flaky Multi-Match  [official]

When a page has multiple elements matching the same role (e.g., two "Submit" buttons — one in
a modal, one in a background form), locators that select by role alone non-deterministically
match either element. `.and()` chains additional filter criteria on the same element, scoping
the locator to the intended target without using positional selectors that break on layout
changes.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('modal form submission does not trigger background form', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'New record' }).click();

  // Two 'Submit' buttons exist: one inside the modal, one in the background form.
  // getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }) is ambiguous — matches both.
  // FRAGILE approach (positional — breaks if layout changes):
  // await page.locator('dialog button:has-text("Submit")').click();

  // STABLE approach: .and() restricts to the exact intersection of both filters.
  // Both conditions must match the SAME DOM element for the locator to resolve.
  const modalSubmit = page
    .getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })
    .and(page.locator('[aria-modal="true"] button, dialog button'));

  await expect(modalSubmit).toBeEnabled();
  await modalSubmit.click();

  // Verify modal closes and background form remains untouched.
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).not.toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('background-form')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**When to use:** Any page with duplicate role-accessible names in multiple contexts (modals,
drawer panels, inline editing forms). Prefer `.and()` over `nth()` — `nth()` is an implicit
positional selector that silently changes behavior if the DOM order changes.

[official] Playwright docs confirm `.and()` requires both conditions to resolve to the SAME
element — it does not filter a list by a second locator. If the two locators resolve to
different elements, the result is empty.

---

### Pattern 163 — Vitest `sequence.shuffle.seed` Pinning for Order-Dependent Failure Reproduction  [community]

When `shuffle: true` reveals an order-dependent test failure in CI, reproducing it locally
requires the same shuffle seed. Vitest emits the seed in the reporter output (`Shuffle seed: 42`)
but it is easy to miss in long CI logs. Pinning the seed in a targeted re-run config file
provides a reproducible local command that requires no CLI flag memorization.

```typescript
// vitest.repro.config.ts — temporary file for reproducing order-dependent failure
// Usage: npx vitest --config vitest.repro.config.ts
// IMPORTANT: Add to .gitignore — this is a debugging artifact, not production config.
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

// Seed extracted from failed CI run output: "Shuffle seed: 1748276400"
const REPRO_SEED = 1748276400;

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    // Reproduce the exact shuffle order from the failing CI run.
    sequence: {
      shuffle: true,
      seed: REPRO_SEED,
    },
    // Limit to the affected test file to reduce noise.
    include: ['src/modules/cart/**/*.test.ts'],
    // Single worker to eliminate parallelism as a confound.
    maxWorkers: 1,
    minWorkers: 1,
    // Verbose output to see test execution order clearly.
    reporters: ['verbose'],
  },
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `vitest.repro.config.ts` should NEVER be committed as a long-lived file — it is
a debugging artifact. Add it to `.gitignore` locally, or create it with a `git stash`
workflow. If committed, future CI runs that use it will have a hard-coded seed and will NOT
be randomized, defeating the shuffle's purpose.

[community] Teams that surface the seed in a PR comment (via the `getSeed()` + globalSetup
pattern from Pattern 149) report that order-dependent failures are reproduced within 5 minutes
versus 20-30 minutes of trial-and-error seed guessing.

---

### Pattern 164 — Playwright `page.route()` Abort Pattern for Selective Third-Party Request Blocking  [community]

Third-party scripts (analytics, customer support widgets, A/B testing platforms) are a
leading cause of E2E flakiness: they introduce unpredictable network latency, modify the DOM,
and compete for CPU during test interactions. Blocking them via `page.route()` with `abort()`
creates a hermetic test environment without requiring proxy configuration or DNS overrides.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Third-party domains to block. Maintained in one place so that additions
// to the app's analytics stack are also blocked in tests automatically.
const THIRD_PARTY_PATTERNS = [
  '**/cdn.segment.io/**',
  '**/www.googletagmanager.com/**',
  '**/intercom.io/**',
  '**/static.hotjar.com/**',
  '**/sentry.io/api/**',           // Block error reporting — reduces CI noise
  '**/featureflags.launchdarkly.com/**', // Block unless testing flag behavior
];

test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
  for (const pattern of THIRD_PARTY_PATTERNS) {
    // route.abort() is synchronous — no async overhead after route registration.
    await page.route(pattern, (route) => route.abort());
  }
});

test('checkout form submits without third-party script interference', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4111 1111 1111 1111');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByText('Payment successful')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Blocking `featureflags.launchdarkly.com` means feature flags default to their
SDK fallback values — tests that depend on flag-controlled behavior will test the fallback,
not the live flag value. Maintain a separate `flag-controlled.spec.ts` suite that allows
LaunchDarkly through, or mock the flag SDK at the module level.

[community] A common mistake is blocking analytics in E2E tests but NOT in component tests,
causing analytics libraries' global error handler to fire in component test environments and
swallow test errors before Vitest sees them. Apply the blocking strategy consistently across
all test tiers.

---

### Pattern 165 — Vitest `onConsole` Reporter Hook for Flakiness-Signal Console Error Detection  [community]

Flaky tests often emit console errors before failing — but the connection between the error
and the test failure is lost when CI truncates logs. A custom reporter that captures `console.error`
calls per-test and attaches them to the test result provides the "last mile" context needed to
diagnose intermittent failures without a local reproduction.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — custom reporter for console error capture
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
import type { Reporter, TestResult, RunnerTask } from 'vitest';

class ConsoleErrorCollector implements Reporter {
  private errors = new Map<string, string[]>();

  onConsole(log: { type: string; content: string; taskId?: string }) {
    if (log.type === 'stderr' || log.content.startsWith('[ERROR]')) {
      const list = this.errors.get(log.taskId ?? '') ?? [];
      // Cap at 10 per test to prevent memory growth in large suites.
      if (list.length < 10) {
        list.push(`[${new Date().toISOString()}] ${log.content.trim()}`);
        this.errors.set(log.taskId ?? '', list);
      }
    }
  }

  onTaskUpdate(packs: [string, TestResult | undefined][]) {
    for (const [id, result] of packs) {
      if (result?.state === 'fail') {
        const captured = this.errors.get(id) ?? [];
        if (captured.length > 0) {
          process.stdout.write(
            `\n  Captured console.error for task ${id}:\n` +
            captured.map((e) => `    ${e}`).join('\n') + '\n'
          );
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    reporters: ['default', new ConsoleErrorCollector()],
  },
});
```

**Tradeoff:** The `onConsole` hook fires for ALL tests. On a 1000-test suite with chatty
components, the error map can grow large. Cap stored errors per test (shown as 10 above) and
filter out known-noisy third-party library prefixes (e.g., skip `[React Query]` debug logs).

[community] Teams that added console error capture to their reporters discovered that 30-40%
of their "mystery flakiness" had a preceding `console.error: React state update on unmounted
component` that was invisible in CI logs — pointing to async cleanup issues, not timing issues.

---

### Anti-Patterns (Cycle 26)

#### AP69 — Using `vi.setSystemTime()` Without Resetting in `afterEach`  [community]
**What:** Calling `vi.setSystemTime(new Date('2026-01-01'))` inside a test to control
date-dependent logic, but not restoring it in `afterEach`. If the test suite runs in a single
worker thread, subsequent tests see the frozen date from the previous test.
**Why harmful:** Tests that call `new Date()` or `Date.now()` after the frozen-time test
implicitly depend on the previous test's time — creating order-dependent flakiness that is
invisible when tests run in isolation. Always pair `vi.setSystemTime()` with
`vi.useRealTimers()` in `afterEach`, or use `vi.useFakeTimers({ now: ... })` which scopes
the fake date to the fake timer session.

#### AP70 — Playwright `waitForSelector` With CSS Selector for Dynamic Class Names  [community]
**What:** Using `page.waitForSelector('.btn-primary.is-loading')` to wait for a loading state,
where `btn-primary` and `is-loading` are generated by a CSS module system (e.g.,
`button_btn-primary_a1b2c3`).
**Why harmful:** CSS module class names contain a content hash that changes on every rebuild.
Tests pass in development (hash is stable between saves) but fail in CI after a clean build
produces a new hash. Switch to `page.getByRole()`, `data-testid`, or `aria-label` — none of
these depend on the CSS build pipeline.

#### AP71 — Sharing a Single MSW Worker Instance Across All Test Files Without Resetting Handlers  [community]
**What:** Creating a single `setupServer()` instance in a shared module and starting it in a
`beforeAll` at the module level, with individual tests adding handlers via `server.use()`.
Handlers added with `server.use()` persist for the lifetime of the worker unless explicitly
removed.
**Why harmful:** Test file B's "add user handler" leaks into Test file C because the shared
server accumulates handlers. File execution order determines whether file C sees the leaked
handler — flakiness that only manifests under parallel execution or when run in a different
sequence. Fix: call `server.resetHandlers()` in `afterEach` to clear test-added handlers, and
`server.restoreHandlers()` in `afterAll` to restore the baseline config.

---

### Real-World Gotchas (Cycle 26)  [community]

**Gotcha 71 — Playwright `locator.filter()` With `hasText` Matches Hidden Text Content**  [community]
`page.getByRole('listitem').filter({ hasText: 'Draft' })` matches list items containing the
text "Draft" anywhere — including text in `aria-hidden` elements and CSS `::before`/`::after`
pseudo-content. On pages that add status badges via CSS `content: "Draft"`, this filter can
match items that visually appear to have a different status. Use `{ hasText: /^Draft$/ }` with
a regex anchored to the visible text, or combine with `getByRole('status')` to match only the
semantic status element.

**Gotcha 72 — Vitest `vi.mock()` Factory Executed Before `beforeAll` on Windows**  [community]
Vitest hoists `vi.mock()` calls to the top of the file during compilation. On Windows with
certain TypeScript configurations, the module resolution order inside the mock factory can
differ from macOS/Linux when the factory imports types from the same module being mocked. This
causes `undefined` factory results — the mock returns `undefined` instead of the mock
implementation — intermittently on Windows CI runners. Fix: use
`vi.mock('module', async () => ({ default: vi.fn() }))` with an `async` factory to ensure the
import inside the factory is fully resolved before the mock is applied.

**Gotcha 73 — Playwright `page.evaluate()` Returning `undefined` for Non-Serializable Values**  [community]
`page.evaluate(() => document.querySelector('.spinner'))` returns `null` (not the element
handle) because DOM nodes are not JSON-serializable. Tests that check the return value of
`page.evaluate()` for DOM state silently receive `undefined` or `null` even when the element
exists. The symptom is a flaky test that sometimes asserts correctly (because it actually
checks a serializable attribute from the element before `evaluate` was incorrectly used) and
sometimes fails (when the DOM structure changes subtly). Use `page.locator()` with web-first
assertions instead of `page.evaluate()` for DOM presence checks.

**Gotcha 74 — Vitest Type-Only Import Removal Causes Mock to Reference Undefined Class**  [community]
When a mock factory uses `import type { MyService } from './service'` (type-only import) to
define the return type of a `vi.fn()`, TypeScript correctly removes the `import` at compile
time. But if the test body then uses the real `MyService` constructor in an assertion like
`expect(instance).toBeInstanceOf(MyService)`, the class reference is `undefined` at runtime
because the type-only import was stripped. The test passes when run in isolation (the class
is loaded via another import) but fails when run in a worker where the module is not otherwise
imported. Fix: use `import { MyService } from './service'` (value import) in the test body,
not `import type`.

**Gotcha 75 — Playwright `response.json()` Called After the Response Body Is Already Consumed**  [community]
When using `page.waitForResponse()` and then calling `await response.json()` inside the
callback AND outside the callback, the second `response.json()` call throws because the body
stream is already consumed. Tests that log responses for debugging frequently fall into this
pattern — the logging call in `afterEach` consumes the body before the assertion in the test
body can read it. Fix: store the parsed JSON in a variable inside the `waitForResponse`
callback and read from the variable everywhere else.

| Symptom | Likely Root Cause | Pattern/Fix | Anti-Pattern to Avoid |
|---------|-------------------|-------------|----------------------|
| Integration test retries mask real assertion failures | Global `retry` config applies to all error types | Pattern 152 (`retry.condition` regex scoped to network errors) | Broad `retry: 2` without condition filter |
| Timeout on slow test inconsistent between CI environments | Hard-coded `setTimeout` value decoupled from base config | Pattern 153 (`test.slow()` 3x adaptive timeout multiplier) | `test.setTimeout(90_000)` hardcoded per-test |
| Eventually-consistent state assertion fails intermittently | Manual polling loop without diff-quality failure messages | Pattern 154 (`expect.poll()` with interval backoff) | `while` loop polling + `waitForTimeout()` |
| Shared S3-mock flaky under concurrent bucket creation | Single test run not confirming idempotency | Pattern 155 (`repeats: 4` + `retry: 2` audit gate) | Merging `repeats > 0` tests to main branch |
| CI retry doubles teardown cost — DB purge runs twice | `afterEach` teardown not conditional on final attempt | Pattern 156 (`testInfo.retry < project.retries` skip expensive cleanup) | Same expensive cleanup on every retry attempt |
| Retry util returns wrong result on N-th attempt in test | `mockImplementationOnce` queue not reset between tests | Pattern 157 (`mockReset()` in `beforeEach` + sequence assertions) | No `mockReset()` — stale mock queue leaks |
| E2E test hangs on `networkidle` when analytics is enabled | Background telemetry prevents idle state | Pattern 158 (`expect(locator).toBeVisible()` instead of `networkidle`) | `waitForLoadState('networkidle')` on analytics-heavy pages |
| Slow tests not surfaced until they timeout on CI | No slow-test threshold reporting | Pattern 159 (`slowTestThreshold` + `onTestSlowness` CI annotations) | No threshold monitoring — discover slow tests only after timeout |
| Auth token incomplete in `storageState` snapshot | Snapshot taken before server-side session established | Pattern 160 (wait for post-auth UI element before `storageState()`) | `waitForURL('/dashboard')` as sole auth readiness signal |
| OpenTelemetry SDK breaks when fake timers active | `vi.useFakeTimers()` fakes `performance` used by OTEL | Pattern 161 (`toFake: ['setTimeout', 'Date']` targeted replacement) | `vi.useFakeTimers()` with no `toFake` restriction |
| Two "Submit" buttons cause non-deterministic click target | Ambiguous role locator matches multiple elements | Pattern 162 (`.and()` intersection locator for disambiguation) | `nth(0)` positional selector — breaks on DOM order changes |
| Order-dependent failure not reproducible without seed | Seed lost in CI log truncation | Pattern 163 (`vitest.repro.config.ts` with pinned seed) | Guessing seed by trial-and-error re-runs |
| Third-party scripts cause intermittent DOM interference | Analytics/support scripts modify DOM during test | Pattern 164 (`page.route()` abort for third-party domains) | No blocking — every run depends on third-party script load time |
| Console errors before flaky failure invisible in CI | `console.error` not captured per-test in reporter | Pattern 165 (`onConsole` reporter hook with per-test error map) | Relying on CI log truncation to surface console errors |
| `vi.setSystemTime()` leaks frozen date to subsequent tests | No `vi.useRealTimers()` in `afterEach` | AP69 (always restore real timers after fake-time test) | Leaving `setSystemTime` active after test completes |
| CSS module class name locator breaks after rebuild | CSS hash changes on clean build | AP70 (`getByRole()` / `data-testid` instead of CSS class selectors) | `waitForSelector('.btn-primary.is-loading')` with hash-dependent class |
| MSW server handlers accumulate across test files | `server.use()` without `resetHandlers()` | AP71 (`server.resetHandlers()` in `afterEach`) | Shared MSW server without per-test handler reset |
