### Pattern 263 — Playwright `page.unrouteAll()` for Test-Scoped Route Cleanup  [official]

Routes registered with `page.route()` accumulate across test setup hooks if they are not explicitly removed. When a fixture or `beforeAll` block registers a catch-all handler and a later test registers a conflicting specific handler, the order of handler evaluation is last-registered-wins — and that order can be non-deterministic across test files in parallel mode. `page.unrouteAll()` removes all handlers registered on the page in a single call, ensuring a clean slate for the next test without needing to track which patterns were registered.

```typescript
// fixtures/api-fixtures.ts — encapsulated route cleanup via fixture
import { test as baseTest } from '@playwright/test';

interface ApiRouteFixture {
  mockProductsApi: (products: object[]) => Promise<void>;
}

export const test = baseTest.extend<ApiRouteFixture>({
  mockProductsApi: async ({ page }, use) => {
    const mockFn = async (products: object[]) => {
      // Register a route for the products API endpoint.
      await page.route('**/api/products**', route =>
        route.fulfill({ json: products })
      );
    };

    await use(mockFn);

    // Teardown: remove ALL routes registered on this page.
    // Ensures no route from this test leaks into the next test's setup phase.
    await page.unrouteAll({ behavior: 'wait' });
    // 'wait' ensures any in-flight route handler invocations complete first.
  },
});

// product-list.test.ts — routes are cleaned up automatically after each test
import { test } from '../fixtures/api-fixtures';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('shows product list from mocked API', async ({ page, mockProductsApi }) => {
  await mockProductsApi([{ id: 1, name: 'Widget', price: 9.99 }]);
  await page.goto('/products');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('product-name').first()).toHaveText('Widget');
  // After this test: fixture teardown calls unrouteAll({ behavior: 'wait' }).
  // Next test starts with zero routes.
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** A fixture or helper registers routes that must not leak into subsequent tests — especially when using `beforeAll`/`afterAll` scope where the page outlives individual test cases.
- **Do NOT use when:** Each test creates a fresh `page` fixture (Playwright's default) — page disposal automatically removes all routes. Manual cleanup is only needed when the page is shared across tests.
- **Alternative:** `browserContext.unrouteAll()` for context-level cleanup when multiple pages in the same context share routes.

[official]

### Pattern 264 — MSW `server.boundary()` API for Per-Test Handler Scope Without `resetHandlers()`  [community]

MSW v2.4+ introduced `server.boundary()`, which creates a scoped handler context. Handlers registered inside a boundary are automatically removed when the boundary's dispose function is called, without affecting the baseline handlers. This is a cleaner alternative to the `server.use()` + `afterEach(server.resetHandlers)` pattern, because the boundary is lexically scoped to the test — there is no risk of forgetting to reset, and handlers from different concurrent tests cannot interfere.

```typescript
// src/__tests__/checkout.test.ts
import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';
import { server } from '../mocks/server';
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { CheckoutPage } from '../CheckoutPage';

describe('CheckoutPage — payment scenarios', () => {
  test('shows error when payment gateway returns 402', async () => {
    // server.boundary() creates a scoped context — handlers registered here
    // are removed when dispose() is called, regardless of test outcome.
    // TypeScript 5.2+ 'using' keyword calls boundary.dispose() automatically on scope exit.
    using boundary = server.boundary();

    boundary.use(
      http.post('/api/payment', () =>
        HttpResponse.json(
          { error: 'Payment declined' },
          { status: 402 }
        )
      )
    );

    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<CheckoutPage />);

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' }));
    await expect(screen.findByText('Payment declined')).resolves.toBeInTheDocument();
    // 'using' exits here: boundary.dispose() removes the 402 handler automatically.
    // No afterEach(server.resetHandlers) needed — boundary is self-cleaning.
  });

  test('shows success banner on 200 payment response', async () => {
    // Different test, different boundary — no state from the 402 test leaks here.
    using boundary = server.boundary();

    boundary.use(
      http.post('/api/payment', () =>
        HttpResponse.json({ orderId: 'ORD-001', status: 'paid' })
      )
    );

    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<CheckoutPage />);

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' }));
    await expect(screen.findByText('Order confirmed')).resolves.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** Test suites that override MSW handlers on a per-test basis and have had bugs caused by missing `afterEach(server.resetHandlers())` calls.
- **Do NOT use when:** Tests that require handler overrides to persist across multiple `test()` blocks. Use `server.use()` + `afterAll(server.resetHandlers)` for that case.
- **Alternative:** `server.use()` + `afterEach(server.resetHandlers())` — the classic pattern; still works but requires discipline to not forget the reset.

[community]

---

### Pattern 265 — Jest 30 `globalsCleanup: 'on'` for Cross-File Global State Leak Prevention  [official]

Jest 30 introduces `globalsCleanup` mode in `testEnvironmentOptions`. When set to `'on'`, Jest automatically clears global properties added during a test file's execution before the next file runs. This prevents the class of flakiness where one test file attaches something to `globalThis` (a mock service, a singleton, a polyfill) and the next file — running in the same V8 context due to shared workers — sees the polluted global. Before Jest 30, the only solution was `jest.resetModules()` combined with manual cleanup, which was easy to forget.

```typescript
// jest.config.ts — enable strict global cleanup between test files
import type { Config } from 'jest';

const config: Config = {
  testEnvironmentOptions: {
    // 'on': cleanup ALL new globals added during a test file's execution.
    // 'soft' (default): only cleanup globals explicitly registered with protectProperties().
    // 'off': no cleanup — legacy behavior for projects with intentional global sharing.
    globalsCleanup: 'on',
  },
  // Combine with clearMocks to also reset mock state between tests.
  clearMocks: true,
};

export default config;
```

```typescript
// Example: globalThis pollution that globalsCleanup: 'on' catches
// file-a.test.ts — attaches a mock to globalThis
import { test, expect } from '@jest/globals';
import { protectProperties } from 'jest-util';

test('registers analytics singleton on globalThis', () => {
  (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)['__analytics__'] = {
    track: jest.fn(),
  };
  expect((globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)['__analytics__']).toBeDefined();
  // Without globalsCleanup: 'on', this global persists into file-b.test.ts.
  // With globalsCleanup: 'on', it is automatically removed after this file completes.
});

// file-b.test.ts — should not see the global from file-a
test('globalThis does not contain analytics singleton from another file', () => {
  // With globalsCleanup: 'on', this assertion passes — the global was cleaned up.
  // Without it, this flakes depending on test file execution order.
  expect((globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)['__analytics__']).toBeUndefined();
});

// If a global SHOULD persist (e.g., a polyfill installed in setupFiles):
// use protectProperties() to opt it out of cleanup.
// setupFiles entry:
import { protectProperties } from 'jest-util';
protectProperties(globalThis['ResizeObserver']); // keeps the ResizeObserver mock
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** A Jest suite with multiple test files shares workers and you observe order-dependent failures traced to `globalThis` pollution (console mocks, DOM API polyfills, registry singletons).
- **Do NOT use when:** You intentionally share global state across test files (rare). Use `'soft'` mode and explicitly `protectProperties()` for shared globals.
- **Alternative:** Jest `--runInBand` masks the symptom by running files sequentially; `jest.resetModules()` per file for module-level cleanup; prefer `'on'` mode over manual cleanup.

[official]

## Real-World Gotchas (Cycle 33)  [community]

**Gotcha 103 — `Promise.allSettled()` in Test Setup Silently Swallows Service Initialization Failures**  [community]
Teams use `Promise.allSettled()` in `beforeAll` to start multiple test services concurrently without one failure aborting the rest. The trap: `allSettled()` never rejects — if a service fails to start, the rejected entry sits in the results array unchecked. The test body then runs against an uninitialized service, producing mysterious `ECONNREFUSED` or `undefined is not a function` failures that look like real test bugs rather than setup failures. WHY this is hard to trace: the error from the failed service is not surfaced as a test setup failure — it only appears in the `allSettled` results object that nobody checked. Fix: always check all settled results after `allSettled()` and throw on any rejection: `const failures = results.filter(r => r.status === 'rejected'); if (failures.length > 0) throw new AggregateError(failures.map(f => (f as PromiseRejectedResult).reason), 'Test setup failed');`

**Gotcha 104 — Playwright `waitForResponse()` Promise Created AFTER `click()` Misses Fast Responses**  [community]
The canonical race condition: `await page.click(btn)` fires the network request; the response arrives in under 50ms (common on localhost or fast CI); then `await page.waitForResponse(url)` is called — but the response has already been processed and is no longer in the event queue. The `waitForResponse()` promise then waits until timeout. WHY this catches everyone eventually: the test passes for months (responses are slow enough that the race is rarely lost), then a server-side performance optimization makes responses faster, and the test starts flaking at ~10% rate. Fix: always create the `waitForResponse()` promise BEFORE the action that triggers the request: `const responsePromise = page.waitForResponse(url); await page.click(btn); await responsePromise;`

**Gotcha 105 — Vitest `vi.mock()` in Parallel Tests Shares Mock Registry Across Workers With `isolate: false`**  [community]
Vitest `pool: 'threads'` with `isolate: false` shares the module registry across workers for performance. When tests call `vi.mock()`, the mock registration modifies this shared registry. Worker A's `vi.mock('./payments')` overrides the payments module for ALL workers running in the same thread pool simultaneously. Worker B imports the mocked version instead of the real module, causing test failures that are non-deterministic because the race only manifests when workers happen to share a thread AND worker B imports the module during the window between A's mock registration and A's cleanup. WHY teams hit this: `isolate: false` is commonly recommended in performance guides without mentioning the `vi.mock()` incompatibility. Fix: never combine `pool: 'threads'` with `isolate: false` when tests use `vi.mock()`. Use `pool: 'vmThreads'` (Pattern 203) which provides per-file module isolation without process isolation overhead.

**Gotcha 106 — Jest `fakeTimers` Replaces `queueMicrotask` by Default, Breaking Promise-Resolution Ordering**  [community]
When `jest.useFakeTimers()` is called without specifying `doNotFake`, it replaces `queueMicrotask` with a fake. Production code that schedules microtask work via `queueMicrotask` (e.g., batching React state updates, deferring I/O coalescing) will only execute those microtasks when fake timers are explicitly advanced — they do not execute between `await` boundaries as they would in production. Result: code that batches N writes into one `queueMicrotask` callback appears to process N times (unbatched) in tests because each `queueMicrotask` is treated as a timer that never auto-fires. WHY teams miss this: `queueMicrotask` is rarely mentioned in fake-timer setup guides — most docs focus on `setTimeout` and `Date`. Fix: add `doNotFake: ['queueMicrotask', 'nextTick']` to `jest.useFakeTimers()` options to preserve real microtask semantics.

**Gotcha 107 — Playwright `context.storageState()` Does Not Capture `sessionStorage` — Auth Tokens Lost**  [community]
`context.storageState()` saves cookies and `localStorage`. It does NOT save `sessionStorage`. Single-page applications that store auth tokens in `sessionStorage` (not `localStorage`) have their tokens silently omitted from the saved state file. Tests that load `auth.json` via `storageState` start every test without the auth token and fail with 401 errors. WHY teams are surprised: the docs clearly state `localStorage` is captured — but developers assume `storageState` captures all browser storage without reading the fine print. Fix: change the application's auth token storage from `sessionStorage` to `localStorage` (or use HttpOnly cookies), OR inject the token at test startup via `page.evaluate(() => sessionStorage.setItem('token', process.env.TEST_AUTH_TOKEN!))` in a `beforeEach`.

**Gotcha 108 — `AbortController` Signal Not Passed to `fetch()` — Aborted Request Completes and Corrupts Later Tests**  [community]
Teams add `AbortController` + `AbortSignal.timeout()` to test helpers to bound async operations but forget to pass the `signal` to `fetch()`. The `AbortController.abort()` call rejects the Promise chain, but the underlying `fetch()` continues running in the background — holding a socket open and occasionally completing and modifying test state AFTER the test has moved on. In integration tests with real HTTP, the orphaned `fetch()` can complete during a SUBSEQUENT test's `beforeEach` and corrupt its mocked response handler state. WHY this is hard to find: the race only manifests when a slow response completes during the next test's setup, not during the test that originally aborted it. Fix: always pass the signal to the `fetch()` call: `fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal })` — without this, abort only cancels downstream Promise chains, not the underlying TCP connection.

| Symptom | Likely Root Cause | Pattern/Fix | Anti-Pattern to Avoid |
|---------|-------------------|-------------|----------------------|
| Video artifact empty when flaky test hangs and times out | Archived video not written on incomplete runs | Pattern 251 (`page.screencast` streaming — writes frames in real time) | `video: 'on'` with test timeouts that prevent archive flush |
| DB connection state leaks between Vitest integration tests | Per-test fixture teardown not type-aware; cleanup skipped on throw | Pattern 252 (`test.extend` lifecycle hooks — teardown guaranteed even on failure) | `beforeEach`/`afterEach` DB setup without fixture ownership |
| ESM singleton with top-level `await` not reset between Jest tests | `jest.resetModules()` unsafe on async-init modules | Pattern 253 (`jest.isolateModulesAsync()` for async ESM singleton reset) | `jest.resetModules()` on async-init modules — partial state risk |
| Locator intermittently matches stale alert node from previous navigation | Broad role locator hits detached or hidden DOM remnants | Pattern 254 (`locator.filter({ hasNot })` — excludes stale/error-state matches) | `getByRole('alert').first()` — positional selector fragile to DOM order |
| CI suite hangs forever — all tests green but worker never exits | Leaked timer or open file handle not detected | Pattern 255 (`--detect-async-leaks` Vitest flag — surfaces leak source + line number) | `--forceExit` — masks the leak, does not fix it |
| Eventually-consistent background queue state not awaitable via locator | State change triggered by backend job, no DOM reflection yet | Pattern 256 (`expect.poll()` with interval backoff — retries custom async callback) | `page.waitForTimeout(5000)` — arbitrary sleep with no condition |
| `requestAnimationFrame` tests use magic `16ms` constant — breaks on frame rate change | `jest.advanceTimersByTime(16)` coupled to assumed frame duration | Pattern 257 (`jest.advanceTimersToNextFrame()` — frame-semantic advancement) | Hard-coded `advanceTimersByTime(1000/60)` |
| CSS-class locator breaks after bundler rebuild changes hash | Hash-based class names change on clean build | Pattern 258 (`page.pickLocator()` interactive audit — identify role/aria locator) | `.btn-primary-hash123` CSS class locators |
| API response assertions miss field renames — tests stay green after breaking change | `toEqual(expect.objectContaining(...))` ignores missing required fields | Pattern 259 (`expect.schemaMatching(ZodSchema)` — validates full structure) | `expect.objectContaining` with only a subset of required fields |
| `Promise.allSettled()` in `beforeAll` swallows service startup error | `allSettled` never rejects — failures silently ignored | Gotcha 103 (always check all settled results; throw `AggregateError` on any rejection) | `await Promise.allSettled([...])` without inspecting `rejected` entries |
| `waitForResponse()` hangs forever on localhost — test passes then flakes | Fast response arrives before `waitForResponse()` is awaited | Gotcha 104 (create `waitForResponse` BEFORE triggering action — never after `click()`) | `await click(); const resp = await waitForResponse()` — response already gone |
| `vi.mock()` in parallel tests corrupts sibling worker's module — non-deterministic | `isolate: false` + `pool: threads` shares module registry | Gotcha 105 (`pool: 'vmThreads'` for per-file isolation with `vi.mock()`) | `isolate: false` with `vi.mock()` in parallel test files |
| Global state from one test file pollutes next file in same Jest worker | `globalThis` mutation not cleaned up between files | Pattern 265 (`globalsCleanup: 'on'` in `testEnvironmentOptions`) | No global cleanup — order-dependent failures surface only with specific file ordering |

### Pattern 266 — Vitest `retry` Object With `condition` Predicate for Error-Gated Retries  [official]

Vitest 4.1 expanded the `retry` option beyond a plain number to accept an object with `count`, `delay`, and `condition` fields. The `condition` predicate receives the thrown `Error` and returns `true` only if that error class warrants a retry. This prevents the anti-pattern of retrying assertion failures (which should fail immediately) while still retrying infrastructure errors (timeouts, connection resets). The `delay` field inserts a deterministic pause between attempts, which is essential when retrying rate-limited external services.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — structured retry with error-gated condition
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    // Global default: retry once on any error (coarse — prefer per-test for precision)
    retry: 1,
  },
});

// payment-gateway.test.ts — per-test retry only for transient infrastructure errors
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { PaymentGateway } from '../src/PaymentGateway';

describe('PaymentGateway — integration', () => {
  it(
    'authorises a card charge',
    {
      // Only retry when the error is a connection-level failure, not an assertion.
      // A failing expect() produces AssertionError — condition returns false → no retry.
      // A network timeout produces FetchError — condition returns true → retry up to 3×.
      retry: {
        count: 3,
        delay: 500,
        condition: (err: Error) =>
          err.name === 'FetchError' || err.message.includes('ECONNRESET'),
      },
      timeout: 15_000,
    },
    async () => {
      const gw = new PaymentGateway({ endpoint: process.env.GATEWAY_URL! });
      const result = await gw.charge({ cardNumber: '4111111111111111', amount: 10_00 });
      expect(result.status).toBe('approved');
      expect(result.transactionId).toMatch(/^TXN-/);
    },
  );
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** Integration tests hit real or semi-real external endpoints that occasionally return connection errors or 503s; you want retries scoped to infrastructure faults only, not logic bugs.
- **Do NOT use when:** The test is a pure unit test — retry should never hide a deterministic assertion failure in business logic.
- **Alternative:** Mock the external service with MSW (Pattern 4b) to eliminate the need for retries entirely; use `retry: number` (plain) when error discrimination is not required.

[official]

### Pattern 267 — Jest `retryTimes()` With `waitBeforeRetry` + `logErrorsBeforeRetry` for Staged Integration Retries  [official]

Jest `retryTimes()` (circus runner only) gained `waitBeforeRetry` and `logErrorsBeforeRetry` options in Jest 29/30. `waitBeforeRetry` inserts a millisecond delay between attempts, preventing thundering-herd retries against a backing service. `logErrorsBeforeRetry` emits the failure reason before each retry attempt, making CI logs actionable even when the test ultimately passes. Without these options, retries are silent and immediate — hiding the error from the CI log entirely.

```typescript
// orders.integration.test.ts — staged retry with logged errors and wait between attempts
// Must use jest-circus runner (default since Jest 27)

import { createOrderService, type OrderService } from '../src/OrderService';

// Top-level declaration — applies to all tests in this file.
// logErrorsBeforeRetry: true surfaces connection errors in CI logs even on eventual pass.
// waitBeforeRetry: 800 prevents hammering a recovering service.
jest.retryTimes(3, {
  logErrorsBeforeRetry: true,
  waitBeforeRetry: 800,
});

let svc: OrderService;

beforeAll(() => {
  svc = createOrderService({ db: process.env.TEST_DB_URL! });
});

afterAll(async () => {
  await svc.close();
});

test('places an order and emits OrderPlaced event', async () => {
  const order = await svc.place({ userId: 'u1', items: ['SKU-A'] });
  expect(order.id).toMatch(/^ORD-/);
  expect(order.status).toBe('pending');
});

test('rejects an order with no items', async () => {
  // This test should never need a retry — it tests pure validation logic.
  // retryTimes at the file level means it will exhaust retries and still fail
  // consistently, correctly marking it as failed rather than masking it.
  await expect(svc.place({ userId: 'u1', items: [] })).rejects.toThrow('items required');
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** A Jest integration test file hits a real or dockerised external service that occasionally suffers cold-start delays or transient connection drops; you want failure reasons visible in CI logs even when retries succeed.
- **Do NOT use when:** You are testing pure business logic — retries mask real failures. Do NOT combine with `retryImmediately: true` for database tests; the immediate retry hits the same locked row.
- **Alternative:** Vitest's `retry` object with `condition` predicate (Pattern 266) provides finer error discrimination; `waitBeforeRetry` alone is often sufficient without `retryImmediately`.

[official]

---

### Pattern 268 — Playwright `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` for Semantic Structure Stability  [official]

Playwright v1.49+ introduced `expect(locator).toMatchAriaSnapshot()`. Unlike DOM snapshot tests or visual diffs, aria snapshots capture the accessibility tree — headings, roles, names, and landmarks — which is structurally stable across CSS changes, icon updates, and DOM refactoring. Aria snapshots eliminate the flakiness class where a pixel-level visual diff or a brittle `.className` selector breaks after a designer changes padding or font. Because the aria tree is driven by semantic HTML and ARIA attributes, it changes only when the component's purpose changes.

```typescript
// checkout.spec.ts — aria snapshot for semantic structure stability
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout page renders correct structure', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Wait for the form to be ready — avoid timing flakiness before snapshot
  await expect(page.getByRole('form', { name: /checkout/i })).toBeVisible();

  // Capture the aria snapshot for the main region only.
  // The snapshot encodes roles and accessible names — CSS changes do not invalidate it.
  // Update the snapshot with: npx playwright test --update-snapshots
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - heading "Checkout" [level=1]
    - region "Order Summary":
      - list:
        - listitem: /Laptop Pro/
    - form "Shipping Address":
      - textbox "Full name"
      - textbox "Address line 1"
      - button "Continue to payment"
  `);
});

test('error state adds alert without removing form fields', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue to payment' }).click();

  // Aria snapshot verifies the error alert appeared AND the form fields still exist.
  // A visual snapshot would break whenever the error styling changes.
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - alert: /Full name is required/
    - form "Shipping Address":
      - textbox "Full name"
  `);
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** You want stable regression tests for UI structure that survive CSS and layout changes; when accessibility compliance is a requirement and you want tests that directly encode semantic intent.
- **Do NOT use when:** The component renders dynamic localised content where aria labels differ per locale — aria snapshots encode label text literally; use YAML wildcards or separate per-locale baselines.
- **Alternative:** `toMatchSnapshot()` on `.innerHTML` is wider but brittle; individual `getByRole` assertions verify elements but do not capture structural relationships.

[official]

---

### Pattern 269 — Playwright `page.addLocatorHandler()` for Automatic Overlay Dismissal  [official]

Playwright v1.42 introduced `page.addLocatorHandler()`, which registers a handler that fires automatically whenever a specified locator becomes visible during any actionability check. This eliminates the most common class of E2E flakiness: intermittent cookie banners, newsletter pop-ups, chat widgets, and "session expiring" alerts that randomly block clicks and produce `TimeoutError` failures. The handler fires before Playwright retries the blocked action, so the test body needs no conditional logic.

```typescript
// fixtures/overlay-handlers.ts — auto-use fixture that dismisses common overlays
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';

export const test = base.extend<{ autoHandleOverlays: void }>({
  autoHandleOverlays: [
    async ({ page }, use) => {
      // Cookie consent banner — dismisses whenever it appears during any action
      await page.addLocatorHandler(
        page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /cookie/i }),
        async (dialog) => {
          await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: /accept|ok/i }).click();
        },
      );

      // Newsletter overlay — closes if it appears between test steps
      await page.addLocatorHandler(
        page.getByTestId('newsletter-modal'),
        async (modal) => {
          await modal.getByRole('button', { name: /no thanks|close/i }).click();
        },
      );

      await use();
      // Handlers are automatically removed when the page is closed after the test
    },
    { auto: true }, // auto-use: applies to every test in this project
  ],
});

// checkout.spec.ts — uses the extended test; overlays handled transparently
test('adds item to cart without being blocked by consent banner', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');
  // If a cookie banner appears here, it is auto-dismissed before click proceeds
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i }).first().click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-count')).toHaveText('1');
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** The application under test renders intermittent overlays (consent dialogs, marketing modals, session-warning banners) that are not part of the feature being tested but randomly block actions.
- **Do NOT use when:** The overlay is the feature under test — use direct locator assertions so its presence/absence is explicitly validated.
- **Alternative:** `page.route()` to block third-party scripts that inject overlays; `page.evaluate()` to set a cookie that suppresses consent banners; both are faster but require knowledge of the overlay's origin.

[official]

---

### Pattern 270 — Jest 30 `workerIdleMemoryLimit` to Prevent OOM-Driven Flakiness  [official]

Large test suites accumulate memory over many test files processed by the same Jest worker. When a worker approaches the OS memory limit, later tests in the batch become unreliable: garbage collection pauses cause timeout failures, and eventual OOM kills produce `SIGKILL`-terminated worker messages that look like network errors. Jest 30 introduced `workerIdleMemoryLimit` to automatically recycle workers whose idle memory exceeds a threshold, resetting heap state before memory pressure causes test failures.

```typescript
// jest.config.ts — memory-limit-driven worker recycling
import type { Config } from 'jest';

const config: Config = {
  // Recycle the worker process when its idle memory exceeds 200 MB.
  // "Idle" means between test files — the worker processes a file, then Jest
  // checks memory before assigning the next file. Exceeding the limit triggers
  // a graceful worker restart (not a kill), so in-flight tests are not affected.
  workerIdleMemoryLimit: '200MB',

  // Give workers extra time to finish cleanup before forced exit.
  // Default 500ms is too short when DB connections are being closed.
  workerGracefulExitTimeout: 3000,

  // Pair with detectOpenHandles to catch the leak source rather than just
  // masking it with recycling. Recycling buys stability; detectOpenHandles
  // gives the root-cause signal to actually fix the leak.
  detectOpenHandles: true,

  // Run fewer files per worker — reduces per-worker memory accumulation
  // as a complement to workerIdleMemoryLimit (not a replacement).
  maxWorkers: '50%',
};

export default config;
```

```typescript
// Example: large snapshot test file that accumulates memory — symptom recycling solves
import { OrderSerializer } from '../src/OrderSerializer';

// Each test allocates ~2MB of serialised strings; accumulates across 50 test files
// until worker memory exceeds the limit and recycling kicks in.
test('serializes order to canonical JSON', () => {
  const orders = Array.from({ length: 200 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: `ORD-${i}`,
    status: 'pending',
    items: [{ sku: `SKU-${i}`, qty: 1 }],
  }));
  const serialized = OrderSerializer.serialize(orders);
  expect(serialized).toMatchSnapshot();
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** CI shows intermittent worker crashes or OOM-adjacent timeout failures in large suites; test files process significant in-memory data (serialisation, image processing, large fixture objects).
- **Do NOT use when:** All tests are fast unit tests with minimal allocation — the recycling overhead costs startup time per worker without benefit.
- **Alternative:** `--runInBand` forces a single process (no worker isolation, but memory is GC-able between files); split large test files into smaller ones to reduce per-file memory peaks.

[official]

### Pattern 271 — Playwright `expect.poll()` With Progressive Intervals for Eventually-Consistent State  [official]

Playwright's `expect.poll()` wraps an arbitrary async callback in a polling loop with configurable `intervals` and `timeout`. It is the correct replacement for any test that currently uses `waitForTimeout()` calls waiting for external state changes (background jobs completing, event consumers catching up, emails arriving in a test inbox). Unlike locator-based web-first assertions, `expect.poll()` can poll any async condition — an HTTP API call, a database query, a Redis key existence check.

```typescript
// order-processing.spec.ts — poll for eventually-consistent fulfilment status
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('background fulfilment job processes order within 30 seconds', async ({ request }) => {
  // Place the order via the API
  const placeResp = await request.post('/api/orders', {
    data: { userId: 'u-test-1', items: [{ sku: 'SKU-A', qty: 2 }] },
  });
  expect(placeResp.ok()).toBeTruthy();
  const { orderId } = await placeResp.json() as { orderId: string };

  // Poll the order status endpoint until 'fulfilled' or timeout.
  // Intervals: check at 500ms, then every 1s, then every 3s (progressive backoff).
  // Replaces the brittle: await page.waitForTimeout(15000)
  await expect.poll(
    async () => {
      const statusResp = await request.get(`/api/orders/${orderId}`);
      const body = await statusResp.json() as { status: string };
      return body.status;
    },
    {
      intervals: [500, 1000, 2000, 3000], // ms between each poll attempt
      timeout: 30_000,
      message: `Order ${orderId} did not reach 'fulfilled' status within 30s`,
    },
  ).toBe('fulfilled');
});

// Pattern also works for event-sourcing projection assertions
test('user projection updates within 10 seconds after event', async ({ request }) => {
  await request.post('/api/events', {
    data: { type: 'UserSignedUp', userId: 'u-42' },
  });

  await expect.poll(
    async () => {
      const resp = await request.get('/api/projections/users/u-42');
      return resp.status();
    },
    { intervals: [200, 500, 1000], timeout: 10_000 },
  ).toBe(200);
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** Testing systems with eventual consistency — background jobs, event-driven pipelines, async notifications, or any state change not triggered by a synchronous HTTP response.
- **Do NOT use when:** The condition is a DOM element state — use Playwright's built-in web-first assertions (`toBeVisible`, `toHaveText`) which already poll the DOM automatically.
- **Alternative:** `waitFor()` in React Testing Library for UI-level polling; `vi.waitFor()` (Vitest, Pattern 275) for Node-level polling in non-Playwright tests.

[official]

### Pattern 272 — Vitest `test.extend` With `onCleanup` Fixture for Guaranteed DB Teardown  [official]

Vitest's `test.extend` builder-pattern fixtures (v4.1+) accept an `onCleanup` callback that runs after the fixture scope ends, even if the test throws. This is strictly safer than `afterEach`/`afterAll` hooks because the cleanup is co-located with the setup code and cannot be accidentally skipped via test file restructuring. For integration tests that create database rows, the fixture guarantees deletion even when an assertion fails mid-test, eliminating the "leftover row from last failure poisons next run" flakiness pattern.

```typescript
// test-utils/fixtures.ts — reusable DB fixtures with guaranteed cleanup
import { test as baseTest } from 'vitest';
import { Pool } from 'pg';

export const test = baseTest
  .extend<{ pool: Pool }>({
    pool: async ({}, { onCleanup }) => {
      const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.TEST_DB_URL });
      onCleanup(async () => {
        await pool.end(); // guaranteed drain — prevents ECONNRESET in next test
      });
      return pool;
    },
  })
  .extend<{ userId: string }>({
    // userId fixture: creates a test user and deletes it after each test.
    // Co-location: setup and cleanup are in the same function — cannot drift apart.
    userId: async ({ pool }, { onCleanup }) => {
      const { rows } = await pool.query<{ id: string }>(
        `INSERT INTO users (name, email)
         VALUES ('Test User', 'test-${Date.now()}@example.com')
         RETURNING id`,
      );
      const id = rows[0].id;
      onCleanup(async () => {
        // Runs even if the test throws — no orphaned rows causing unique-constraint
        // failures in the NEXT test run.
        await pool.query('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = $1', [id]);
      });
      return id;
    },
  });

// orders.test.ts — uses fixtures; cleanup is automatic and failure-safe
import { test } from './test-utils/fixtures';
import { expect } from 'vitest';

test('creates an order for a valid user', async ({ pool, userId }) => {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<{ id: string }>(
    `INSERT INTO orders (user_id, status) VALUES ($1, 'pending') RETURNING id`,
    [userId],
  );
  expect(rows[0].id).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f-]+$/);
  // If this assertion fails, onCleanup still runs — order AND user rows are deleted.
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** Integration tests create real database rows (or any persistent external state) and you need bulletproof teardown regardless of test outcome; especially in suites run with high parallelism where leftover rows create constraint violations.
- **Do NOT use when:** All dependencies are in-memory mocks — fixture overhead adds complexity without benefit for unit tests.
- **Alternative:** Transaction-rollback pattern (Pattern 67, `aroundEach`) if the DB supports transactions; `afterEach` hooks are acceptable for simple cases but must be manually kept in sync with setup.

[official]

---

### Pattern 273 — Jest 30 `globalsCleanup: 'on'` With `protectProperties()` for Selective Global Retention  [official]

Jest 30's `globalsCleanup: 'on'` (in `testEnvironmentOptions`) wipes globalThis additions between test files, eliminating cross-file global state leaks. The complementary `protectProperties()` function from `jest-util` allows intentional shared globals (polyfills, JSDOM patches, test-time registry singletons) to survive cleanup. The combination gives teams a zero-leak default with a surgical escape hatch — avoiding the all-or-nothing choice between `'on'` (strict) and `'off'` (no protection).

```typescript
// jest.config.ts — enable strict global cleanup
import type { Config } from 'jest';

const config: Config = {
  testEnvironment: 'jsdom',
  testEnvironmentOptions: {
    // 'on': every globalThis property added by a test file is removed after that file.
    // 'soft': only properties not in the original env are removed (default).
    // Default 'soft' is not strict enough for large suites with shared workers.
    globalsCleanup: 'on',
  },
  setupFilesAfterFramework: ['<rootDir>/jest.setup.ts'],
};

export default config;

// jest.setup.ts — install polyfills that must survive globalsCleanup: 'on'
import { protectProperties } from 'jest-util';

// ResizeObserver is not in jsdom — install a mock and protect it from cleanup.
// Without protectProperties(), globalsCleanup: 'on' would remove this mock after
// the first test file, breaking all subsequent files that rely on it.
class ResizeObserverMock {
  observe() {}
  unobserve() {}
  disconnect() {}
}
(globalThis as typeof globalThis & { ResizeObserver: unknown }).ResizeObserver = ResizeObserverMock;
protectProperties((globalThis as typeof globalThis & { ResizeObserver: unknown }).ResizeObserver);

// IntersectionObserver polyfill — same pattern
(globalThis as typeof globalThis & { IntersectionObserver: unknown }).IntersectionObserver = class {
  observe() {}
  unobserve() {}
  disconnect() {}
};
protectProperties(
  (globalThis as typeof globalThis & { IntersectionObserver: unknown }).IntersectionObserver,
);
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** A Jest suite with many parallel workers shows order-dependent failures traced to `globalThis` mutations (analytics singletons, custom event bus registrations, DOM API polyfills installed per-file).
- **Do NOT use when:** The suite relies heavily on shared global state by design (legacy jQuery-style suites) — switching to `'on'` requires auditing all cross-file global dependencies first.
- **Alternative:** `resetModules: true` cleans the module registry (not globalThis); `jest.isolateModules()` per-test for module-level state; `'soft'` mode as a stepping stone before full `'on'`.

[official]

---

### Pattern 274 — Playwright `tracing.group()` for Structured Flakiness Investigation  [official]

Playwright v1.49 added `tracing.group()` to visually cluster related actions in the trace viewer. When a flaky test is diagnosed using a trace file, ungrouped action lists of 50+ entries are hard to navigate. Grouping actions by logical operation (login, navigate, assert) reduces diagnosis time from minutes to seconds by localising the failure to a named cluster. `tracing.group()` is especially valuable in parametrised tests where the same action sequence repeats with different data — each group label shows which data set triggered the failure.

```typescript
// auth-flow.spec.ts — grouped trace for multi-step E2E with flakiness diagnosis
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('user logs in and sees dashboard', async ({ page, context }) => {
  const tracing = context.tracing;

  // Group: authentication steps — collapsed in trace viewer unless this group fails
  await tracing.group('Login flow');
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('alice@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('secret-test-pw');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/dashboard');
  await tracing.groupEnd();

  // Group: dashboard assertion — isolates assertion failures from navigation failures
  await tracing.group('Dashboard assertions');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /welcome/i })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('user-greeting')).toContainText('Alice');
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toBeVisible();
  await tracing.groupEnd();

  // Group: data load verification — separate from UI assertions
  await tracing.group('Recent activity load');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('activity-feed')).not.toBeEmpty();
  await tracing.groupEnd();
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** E2E tests have more than 10-15 actions; tests are parametrised with multiple data sets; flakiness diagnosis is slowed by unstructured action lists in trace files.
- **Do NOT use when:** Simple tests with 3-5 actions — grouping adds code without meaningful trace navigation benefit.
- **Alternative:** `test.step()` provides the same grouping in the HTML report and is the standard mechanism; `tracing.group()` is the lower-level API used when trace grouping is needed outside of `test.step()` boundaries.

[official]

### Pattern 275 — Vitest `vi.waitFor()` for Polling Arbitrary Async Conditions  [official]

Vitest introduced `vi.waitFor()` as a counterpart to Playwright's `expect.poll()` for Node-side test assertions. It repeatedly calls a callback until it stops throwing (or until timeout), making it the correct tool for testing eventually-consistent state in non-browser environments. The common misuse is a `setInterval` + `Promise` polling loop that leaks the interval timer if the condition is never met — `vi.waitFor()` handles timeout and cleanup internally.

```typescript
// event-processor.test.ts — poll for eventually-consistent state without timer leaks
import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { EventProcessor } from '../src/EventProcessor';
import { InMemoryEventBus } from '../src/InMemoryEventBus';

describe('EventProcessor', () => {
  let bus: InMemoryEventBus;
  let processor: EventProcessor;

  beforeEach(() => {
    bus = new InMemoryEventBus();
    processor = new EventProcessor(bus);
    processor.start(); // starts background processing loop
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    await processor.stop(); // cleanly drains the queue
  });

  it('processes UserCreated event and emits WelcomeEmail', async () => {
    const emittedEvents: string[] = [];
    bus.onEmit((event) => emittedEvents.push(event.type));

    // Publish the event — processing is async (background loop)
    bus.publish({ type: 'UserCreated', userId: 'u-42', email: 'alice@example.com' });

    // vi.waitFor polls until the assertion passes or times out (default 1000ms).
    // Interval: 100ms below. No leaked timers — vi.waitFor cleans up internally.
    await vi.waitFor(
      () => {
        expect(emittedEvents).toContain('WelcomeEmail');
      },
      { timeout: 5000, interval: 100 },
    );

    // Once vi.waitFor resolves, the assertion is guaranteed to have passed
    expect(emittedEvents.filter((e) => e === 'WelcomeEmail')).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('does not emit WelcomeEmail for system users', async () => {
    const emittedEvents: string[] = [];
    bus.onEmit((event) => emittedEvents.push(event.type));

    bus.publish({ type: 'UserCreated', userId: 'system', email: 'ops@internal' });

    // Use a short timeout for negative assertions — expect the event NOT to appear
    await expect(
      vi.waitFor(
        () => { expect(emittedEvents).toContain('WelcomeEmail'); },
        { timeout: 500, interval: 50 },
      ),
    ).rejects.toThrow();
  });
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** Testing background workers, event consumers, pub/sub systems, or any state that changes asynchronously outside the test's direct control in a Node/Vitest context.
- **Do NOT use when:** The state change is synchronous or directly awaitable — await the operation directly instead of polling.
- **Alternative:** `waitFor()` from `@testing-library/react` for React component state; `expect.poll()` in Playwright (Pattern 271) for browser-side polling; hand-rolled `setInterval` loops are never the right choice (leak risk).

[official]

---

### Pattern 276 — Jest 30 `waitForUnhandledRejections: true` to Surface Swallowed Async Errors  [official]

Jest's default behavior drops unhandled Promise rejections that occur after a test completes but before the next test's `beforeEach`. The result: an async operation started in test A throws an error, the error is silently lost, and test B fails with a mysterious state corruption error. Jest 30's `waitForUnhandledRejections: true` gives the event loop one turn after each test to collect pending rejections and attribute them to the correct test. This converts invisible async errors into correctly-attributed test failures.

```typescript
// jest.config.ts — surface swallowed async failures
import type { Config } from 'jest';

const config: Config = {
  // Give the event loop one extra turn after each test to collect pending
  // unhandled rejections and attach them to the test that produced them.
  // Without this, fire-and-forget Promises that reject appear as noise in
  // the NEXT test's error output, making root-cause analysis difficult.
  waitForUnhandledRejections: true,

  // Pair with detectOpenHandles to catch Promise chains that never resolve
  detectOpenHandles: true,
};

export default config;

// notification.service.test.ts — demonstrates the coverage gap this option fills
import { NotificationService } from '../src/NotificationService';

test('fire-and-forget rejection is attributed to THIS test', () => {
  const svc = new NotificationService({ endpoint: 'http://invalid.test' });
  // BAD production pattern — fire-and-forget notification send.
  // The fetch() rejects asynchronously AFTER this test synchronously returns.
  // Without waitForUnhandledRejections, the rejection is lost or attributed to
  // the NEXT test. With it, Jest waits one tick and attaches it to THIS test.
  svc.sendAsync({ to: 'alice', message: 'hello' });
  // No await — intentional fire-and-forget to demonstrate the issue
  // (this test now correctly FAILS with the fetch rejection error)
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** The test suite includes service code that uses fire-and-forget Promises (notification dispatching, analytics pings, background indexing) and you want those failures to surface as test errors rather than mysterious state corruption in later tests.
- **Do NOT use when:** The suite intentionally tests fire-and-forget patterns where rejection is expected and handled by a process-level `unhandledRejection` listener — this option would then produce false-positive failures.
- **Alternative:** ESLint `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises` rule (Pattern 20) catches missing `await` statically; `process.on('unhandledRejection', ...)` in test setup (Pattern 104) for explicit rejection tracking.

[official]

---

### Pattern 277 — Playwright `page.clock.setFixedTime()` vs `install()` — Choosing the Right Clock API  [official]

Playwright v1.45 introduced `page.clock`, which controls Date, setTimeout, setInterval, and requestAnimationFrame inside the browser page. The two primary APIs are `setFixedTime()` (freezes `Date.now()` without touching timers — lightweight, safe to call anytime) and `install()` (replaces all time APIs — powerful but must be called before navigation or page scripts execute). Confusing these two causes a subtle class of flakiness: calling `install()` after `goto()` leaves the page's already-executed scripts using real timers while newly-executed scripts use fake ones, producing split-world behaviour.

```typescript
// date-display.spec.ts — correct usage of setFixedTime vs install()
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// CASE 1: Only Date.now() needs to be frozen (e.g., relative timestamps: "2 minutes ago")
// Use setFixedTime() — safe to call at any point, does not affect timers or intervals
test('shows relative timestamp correctly', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/activity-feed');
  // setFixedTime is safe AFTER goto() — it only freezes Date.now() / new Date()
  await page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date('2026-05-14T10:00:00.000Z'));

  await expect(page.getByTestId('last-activity')).toHaveText('2 minutes ago');
});

// CASE 2: setTimeout / setInterval / requestAnimationFrame must also be controlled
// Use install() — MUST be called BEFORE page.goto() or the page's scripts run
test('auto-save triggers after 5 seconds of inactivity', async ({ page }) => {
  // install() BEFORE navigation — all time APIs are replaced before any script runs
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-05-14T10:00:00.000Z') });
  await page.goto('/editor');

  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Content' }).fill('Draft text');

  // Advance the fake clock by 5 seconds — triggers the auto-save setTimeout
  await page.clock.tickAsync(5_000);

  await expect(page.getByTestId('save-indicator')).toHaveText('Saved');
});

// ANTI-PATTERN — split-world clocks (commented to prevent linting errors):
// test('broken: install() after goto()', async ({ page }) => {
//   await page.goto('/editor');          // page scripts run with real timers
//   await page.clock.install({ time: … }); // ← too late: existing setTimeouts use real clock
// });
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** Use `setFixedTime()` when only `Date.now()` / `new Date()` needs to be deterministic. Use `install()` when timers, intervals, or animation frames must also be controlled — always call it before `page.goto()`.
- **Do NOT use when:** The page uses third-party scripts that depend on real wall-clock timing (analytics, session tracking) — freezing time breaks those scripts. Scope clock control to components under test.
- **Alternative:** `jest.useFakeTimers()` / `vi.useFakeTimers()` for Node-side timer control; `page.clock.pauseAt()` to pause time at a specific instant without ticking manually.

[official]

---

### Pattern 278 — Playwright `waitForResponse()` Promise Created Before Action to Prevent Response-Race  [official]

A canonical Playwright race condition: the test clicks a button, the page fires a fetch, the server responds in under 50ms, and then the test creates a `waitForResponse()` promise — but the response has already been processed and is no longer in the event queue, so `waitForResponse()` hangs until timeout. Playwright's own best-practices guide documents this explicitly as "always create the response promise BEFORE the action." The fix is straightforward but requires a mental model shift: think of `waitForResponse` as subscribing to a future event, not querying a past one.

```typescript
// api-submit.spec.ts — correct waitForResponse ordering prevents response-race flakiness
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('form submission calls the correct API endpoint', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/contact');
  await page.getByLabel('Name').fill('Alice');
  await page.getByLabel('Message').fill('Hello');

  // CORRECT: subscribe to the response BEFORE the action that triggers the request.
  // Created now; resolves when matching response arrives regardless of server speed.
  const responsePromise = page.waitForResponse(
    (resp) => resp.url().includes('/api/contact') && resp.status() === 200,
  );

  // Trigger the request AFTER the listener is registered
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Send' }).click();

  // Await the promise — guaranteed to resolve even for sub-10ms responses
  const response = await responsePromise;
  expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
  const body = await response.json() as { success: boolean };
  expect(body.success).toBe(true);

  await expect(page.getByTestId('success-message')).toBeVisible();
});

// Same pattern for navigation and request events
test('settings link navigates to settings page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Subscribe before click — works even for sub-10ms SPA navigation
  const navPromise = page.waitForURL('**/settings');
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Settings' }).click();
  await navPromise;

  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Settings' })).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** Asserting on network responses, navigations, or any browser events triggered by a user action — always subscribe before the action, never after.
- **Do NOT use when:** The action does NOT trigger a network request (local state changes, form validation) — `waitForResponse()` would hang until timeout.
- **Alternative:** `page.route()` + `route.fulfill()` to intercept and assert on the request payload without waiting for a real server response; `expect(page).toHaveURL()` for navigation assertions.

[official]

---

### Pattern 279 — Node.js `AsyncLocalStorage` for Per-Concurrent-Test Context Isolation  [community]

When integration tests run concurrently and share a singleton service that stores request context (user ID, correlation ID, transaction ID) in a module-level variable, concurrent tests overwrite each other's context, producing assertion failures that appear random. The correct fix is `AsyncLocalStorage` — Node.js's built-in mechanism for per-async-chain context isolation without requiring process-per-test isolation. Tests that inject context via `AsyncLocalStorage.run()` are fully isolated from sibling tests running in the same worker process.

```typescript
// src/context/request-context.ts — AsyncLocalStorage for per-chain isolation
import { AsyncLocalStorage } from 'async_hooks';

export interface RequestContext {
  userId: string;
  correlationId: string;
  traceId: string;
}

// Single AsyncLocalStorage instance — shared across the process but per-async-chain isolated.
// Each `run()` call creates a new isolated store; reads from sibling chains return undefined.
export const requestContext = new AsyncLocalStorage<RequestContext>();

// src/services/AuditService.ts — reads context from AsyncLocalStorage (no argument threading)
import { requestContext } from '../context/request-context';

export class AuditService {
  async logAction(action: string): Promise<void> {
    const ctx = requestContext.getStore();
    if (!ctx) throw new Error('No request context — must call within requestContext.run()');
    // Records action with userId from the current async chain — never from another test
    console.log(`[AUDIT] ${ctx.userId}: ${action} (trace: ${ctx.traceId})`);
  }
}

// audit-service.test.ts — concurrent tests with isolated contexts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { requestContext } from '../src/context/request-context';
import { AuditService } from '../src/services/AuditService';

const svc = new AuditService();

// These tests run concurrently — each has its OWN AsyncLocalStorage chain.
// Without AsyncLocalStorage, concurrent tests share the module-level userId,
// causing non-deterministic assertion failures when context is overwritten.
describe.concurrent('AuditService concurrent tests', () => {
  it('logs action with Alice context', async () => {
    await requestContext.run(
      { userId: 'user-alice', correlationId: 'corr-001', traceId: 'trace-A' },
      async () => {
        // This assertion is safe even if 'user-bob' test runs simultaneously
        await expect(svc.logAction('view-profile')).resolves.toBeUndefined();
        expect(requestContext.getStore()?.userId).toBe('user-alice');
      },
    );
  });

  it('logs action with Bob context', async () => {
    await requestContext.run(
      { userId: 'user-bob', correlationId: 'corr-002', traceId: 'trace-B' },
      async () => {
        await expect(svc.logAction('edit-profile')).resolves.toBeUndefined();
        expect(requestContext.getStore()?.userId).toBe('user-bob');
      },
    );
  });
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** Concurrent integration tests share a singleton service that reads per-request context (auth, correlation IDs, tenant IDs) from a module-level variable; switching to `AsyncLocalStorage` eliminates the race without forcing sequential execution.
- **Do NOT use when:** Tests are already isolated in separate processes (Vitest `pool: 'forks'`) — process isolation already provides full context separation, and `AsyncLocalStorage` adds complexity without benefit.
- **Alternative:** Dependency injection — pass context as a function argument (stateless service design eliminates the problem entirely); `pool: 'forks'` for maximum isolation at the cost of startup overhead.

[community]

---

### Pattern 280 — Playwright `page.screencast` Live Frame Streaming for Timeout-Crash Evidence  [official]

When a Playwright test times out and the worker is killed, the video archive (`video: 'on'`) is never flushed to disk because the archive operation runs in teardown that is bypassed on timeout. `page.screencast` (introduced in Playwright v1.60) streams frames via a `ReadableStream` so each frame is available immediately rather than buffered until the test ends. A consumer that writes frames to a file in real-time produces a partial but playable video artifact even when the test times out, providing the visual evidence needed to diagnose hangs.

```typescript
// test-utils/streaming-screencast.ts — real-time frame writer for hang evidence
import type { Page } from '@playwright/test';
import { createWriteStream } from 'fs';
import { mkdir } from 'fs/promises';
import { join } from 'path';

/**
 * Starts a live screencast that writes frames in real time.
 * Returns a stop function — call it in a finally block.
 * Partial video is readable even if the test hangs and is killed by timeout.
 */
export async function startStreamingScreencast(
  page: Page,
  testName: string,
): Promise<() => void> {
  const dir = join('test-results', 'screencasts');
  await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
  const safeName = testName.replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/gi, '-').toLowerCase();
  const filePath = join(dir, `${safeName}-live.webm`);
  const writeStream = createWriteStream(filePath);

  const screencast = await page.screencast();
  if (!screencast) return () => {};

  const reader = screencast.getReader();
  let active = true;

  // Consume frames in background — each frame is written immediately
  (async () => {
    try {
      while (active) {
        const { done, value } = await reader.read();
        if (done || !active || !value) break;
        writeStream.write(value);
      }
    } finally {
      writeStream.end();
    }
  })();

  return () => {
    active = false;
    reader.cancel().catch(() => {});
  };
}

// checkout.spec.ts — attach live screencast to long-running tests
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { startStreamingScreencast } from '../test-utils/streaming-screencast';

test('completes multi-step checkout — hang evidence on timeout', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  const stopScreencast = await startStreamingScreencast(page, testInfo.title);

  try {
    await page.goto('/checkout');
    await page.fill('[name="card-number"]', '4111111111111111');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('order-confirmation')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 20_000 });
  } finally {
    stopScreencast(); // stop streaming — partial or full artifact already on disk
  }
});
```

**Use when / Do NOT use when / Alternative:**

- **Use when:** Long-running E2E tests occasionally time out and the standard video artifact is empty because the timeout prevents teardown; you need visual evidence of what the test was doing at the moment of hang.
- **Do NOT use when:** Tests consistently pass or fail within the timeout window — standard `video: 'on-first-retry'` is simpler and sufficient.
- **Alternative:** `trace: 'retain-on-failure-and-retries'` (Pattern 84) captures DOM snapshots and action logs per retry — often more useful than video for non-visual flakiness; screenshot on failure for single-frame evidence.

[official]

---

## Community Gotchas (Cycle 34)  [community]

**Gotcha 109 — `waitFor()` With Multiple Assertions Passes on First Snapshot Where Both Are True, Misses Immediate Re-render**  [community]
`waitFor(() => { expect(A); expect(B); })` retries the callback until it passes without throwing — this is correct when both A and B need to be true simultaneously. The real gotcha is the opposite failure mode: in fast CI environments with React's batched state updates, the component renders A first, then B appears in a subsequent microtask render. `waitFor` catches the first poll where both A and B are true and exits immediately. If a rapid subsequent re-render removes B (e.g., a loading state that flickers), the assertion window closes before the flicker is observable. WHY this surfaces as flakiness: locally the render cycle is slow enough that the window is stable, but in CI the microtask batch executes within the poll interval, making B visible-then-gone within a single `waitFor` interval. Fix: assert A and B in separate `waitFor` calls, or add a stabilisation `await screen.findByRole('...')` that confirms no re-render occurs after both elements are present.

**Gotcha 110 — Vitest `pool: 'vmThreads'` + `import.meta.env` Mutation Persists Across Test Files in Same VM Context**  [community]
Vitest's `vmThreads` pool reuses V8 contexts between test files within a worker to reduce startup time. `import.meta.env` is evaluated once per module load into the VM context. If a test mutates `import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL` directly and the file ends, `vi.resetModules()` re-executes module code but does NOT re-initialize `import.meta.env` — the mutation persists into the next test file loaded into the same V8 context. WHY this is surprising: developers expect module reset to restore env, but env is a non-module global baked into the VM context at creation time. Fix: always use `vi.stubEnv('VITE_API_URL', value)` instead of direct `import.meta.env` mutation — `vi.stubEnv` registers the original value and restores it automatically after each test. Alternatively, switch to `pool: 'forks'` which uses separate OS processes and eliminates the shared-context issue.

**Gotcha 111 — Playwright `test.describe.serial()` Retry Replays Side-Effects — Duplicate DB Rows, Duplicate Emails**  [community]
`test.describe.serial()` groups tests to run sequentially in a single worker. When any test in the group fails, Playwright retries the ENTIRE group from the first test in a fresh worker. If a test earlier in the serial group performs a side-effect (creates a database record, sends an email, initiates a charge) and then the group is retried, the side-effect executes again — potentially creating duplicate records or triggering duplicate notifications. WHY this catches teams: the retry is silent; the duplicate side-effect only manifests in downstream systems (billing records, outbox tables, email counts) that are not checked in the test body. Fix: add idempotency guards to all side-effects in serial tests (upsert instead of insert, deduplication keys on email sends) OR add a `test.beforeAll` that checks for and cleans pre-existing state from a previous retry.

**Gotcha 112 — `AbortSignal.timeout()` Passed to Wrapper But Not Forwarded to Underlying `fetch()` — Orphaned Request Corrupts Next Test**  [community]
`AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` creates a signal that fires after 5 seconds. Developers wrap `fetch()` in a helper that accepts a `signal` option, but the internal implementation creates a NEW `AbortController` internally rather than propagating the provided signal to `fetch()`. The timeout signal fires and rejects the outer Promise chain, but the underlying `fetch()` continues running as an orphaned background task — holding a socket open and occasionally completing and modifying test state AFTER the test has moved on. The orphaned `fetch()` can complete during a SUBSEQUENT test's `beforeEach` and overwrite its mocked response handler state. WHY this is hard to find: the race only manifests when a slow response completes during the next test's setup, not during the test that originally aborted it. Fix: always trace signal propagation through the entire call chain — use `fetch(url, { signal })` and verify with `signal.throwIfAborted()` at each async boundary.

**Gotcha 113 — Jest `--randomize --seed=N` Does Not Fully Reproduce Cross-File Order-Dependency Found in CI**  [community]
Jest `--randomize` shuffles test order WITHIN files using the provided seed. When a cross-file order-dependency flakiness is detected on CI, the developer runs `npx jest --randomize --seed=<N>` locally to reproduce — but the reproduction fails even with the same seed. WHY: `--randomize` only shuffles the within-file test order. The ORDER of test FILES across workers is controlled by `testSequencer`, which uses a separate ordering strategy (often filesystem mtime or alphabetical) that is NOT seeded by `--seed`. So the same seed produces the same within-file shuffle, but the inter-file order differs between the CI run and the local run. Fix: to reproduce a cross-file order-dependency, also capture and replay the file execution order. Specify the two files that interact explicitly: `jest file-a.test.ts file-b.test.ts --randomize --seed=<N>` — specifying files explicitly bypasses `testSequencer` ordering and isolates the inter-file interaction.

### Quick Reference additions (Cycle 34)

| Symptom | Likely Root Cause | Pattern/Fix | Anti-Pattern to Avoid |
|---------|-------------------|-------------|----------------------|
| Vitest integration retry fires on assertion errors, not just infra errors | Plain `retry: 3` retries all errors including `AssertionError` | Pattern 266 (`retry: { condition }` predicate — filter to infrastructure errors only) | `retry: 3` global on unit tests — masks real logic bugs |
| Jest integration retry succeeds but CI log shows no failure detail | `retryTimes()` without `logErrorsBeforeRetry` — errors suppressed | Pattern 267 (`logErrorsBeforeRetry: true` + `waitBeforeRetry` for staged retry) | Silent retries that pass with no logged failure context |
| Playwright snapshot breaks after CSS refactor despite no semantic change | DOM snapshot captures CSS classes, not semantic structure | Pattern 268 (`toMatchAriaSnapshot()` — aria tree stable across CSS changes) | `toMatchSnapshot()` on `.innerHTML` with dynamic class names |
| Cookie banner blocks click intermittently on CI | Cookie consent modal appears at non-deterministic timing | Pattern 269 (`addLocatorHandler()` auto-dismiss on actionability check) | Conditional `if (await banner.isVisible()) banner.close()` — race-prone |
| Jest worker crashes mid-suite with OOM SIGKILL | Large test files accumulate heap; worker hits OS memory limit | Pattern 270 (`workerIdleMemoryLimit: '200MB'` — recycle before pressure) | `--maxWorkers=1` serial run — masks the leak, does not fix it |
| Background job state not assertable — `waitForTimeout(10000)` sleep | Eventually-consistent state has no DOM reflection; requires polling | Pattern 271 (`expect.poll()` with progressive intervals — no timeout waste) | `await page.waitForTimeout(10000)` — arbitrary sleep |
| DB rows from failed test pollute next test run with constraint errors | `afterEach` cleanup skipped when test throws | Pattern 272 (Vitest `test.extend` `onCleanup` — runs even on test failure) | `afterEach(() => db.delete(...))` — skipped on uncaught throws |
| globalThis mock from one test file corrupts another file's assertions | `globalThis` mutation not cleaned between files in shared workers | Pattern 273 (`globalsCleanup: 'on'` + `protectProperties()` for shared polyfills) | No global cleanup — assume workers are always fresh |
| Trace file has 60+ ungrouped actions — impossible to find failure point | No logical grouping in trace; all actions look equal | Pattern 274 (`tracing.group()` / `test.step()` — named clusters in trace viewer) | Flat list of actions with generic names like `click`, `fill` |
| Background EventBus consumer state not assertable — leaking setInterval | Hand-rolled polling loop using `setInterval` leaks on timeout | Pattern 275 (`vi.waitFor()` — internal cleanup on timeout, no timer leak) | `new Promise(resolve => setInterval(checkFn, 100))` — always leaks interval |
| Fire-and-forget service call rejects AFTER test ends — error lost silently | Unhandled rejection arrives post-test; attributed to next test | Pattern 276 (`waitForUnhandledRejections: true` — attach rejection to originating test) | Ignoring rejection in test — surfaces as mysterious next-test failure |
| `page.clock.install()` after `goto()` — some timers use real clock, others fake | `install()` called after page scripts executed; split-world clocks | Pattern 277 (`install()` BEFORE `goto()`; `setFixedTime()` AFTER for Date-only freeze) | `await page.goto(); await page.clock.install()` — undefined timer behaviour |
| `waitForResponse()` hangs on fast localhost — response already processed | Response arrives before `waitForResponse` listener registered | Pattern 278 (create `waitForResponse` promise BEFORE triggering action always) | `await click(); const r = await waitForResponse(url)` — response already gone |
| Concurrent integration tests: wrong userId returned from singleton service | Module-level context variable overwritten by concurrent test | Pattern 279 (`AsyncLocalStorage.run()` for per-chain context isolation) | `let currentUserId: string` module-level — overwritten on concurrent access |
| Video artifact empty for timed-out Playwright test — no visual evidence | `video: 'on'` archive never flushed when worker killed by timeout | Pattern 280 (`page.screencast` streaming — frames written in real time before timeout) | `video: 'on'` only — archive requires clean teardown to flush |
