**Pattern 692** — Playwright v1.54 `annotation.location` for Systematic Quarantine Audit  [official]

Playwright v1.54 added a `location` property to test annotations (the objects emitted by `test.skip()`, `test.fixme()`, `test.fail()`, and `testInfo.annotations`). The `location` contains the source file path and line number where the annotation was added. In a large test suite with dozens of quarantined tests, this is the missing link for systematic review: a custom reporter can emit a `quarantine-report.json` mapping every `test.fixme()` to its file, line, and age — enabling a weekly SLA review without manual grep.

```typescript
// custom-quarantine-reporter.ts — emits quarantine-report.json with location metadata
import type {
  Reporter,
  TestCase,
  TestResult,
  FullResult,
} from '@playwright/test/reporter';
import * as fs from 'node:fs';

interface QuarantineEntry {
  title: string;
  file: string;
  line: number;
  column: number;
  reason: string | undefined;
  addedAt: string | undefined; // extracted from annotation description by convention
}

export default class QuarantineReporter implements Reporter {
  private entries: QuarantineEntry[] = [];

  onTestEnd(test: TestCase, result: TestResult): void {
    // Collect all annotations emitted by test.fixme() / test.skip()
    for (const annotation of result.annotations) {
      if (annotation.type === 'fixme' || annotation.type === 'skip') {
        // annotation.location is available from Playwright v1.54+
        // It is undefined for programmatic annotations added without a call site.
        const loc = annotation.location;
        this.entries.push({
          title: test.titlePath().join(' > '),
          file: loc?.file ?? '(unknown)',
          line: loc?.line ?? 0,
          column: loc?.column ?? 0,
          // Convention: annotation description holds "YYYY-MM-DD: reason"
          reason: annotation.description,
          addedAt: annotation.description?.match(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/)?.[0],
        });
      }
    }
  }

  async onEnd(_result: FullResult): Promise<void> {
    // Sort by file for stable diffs in version control.
    this.entries.sort((a, b) => a.file.localeCompare(b.file) || a.line - b.line);
    fs.writeFileSync(
      'quarantine-report.json',
      JSON.stringify({ generatedAt: new Date().toISOString(), entries: this.entries }, null, 2),
    );
  }
}
```

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — attach the quarantine reporter for CI nightly sweeps
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'node:path';

export default defineConfig({
  reporter: [
    ['html'],
    // Quarantine reporter runs alongside the HTML reporter.
    // In CI: archive quarantine-report.json as an artifact and post
    // a comment on the PR if any quarantine entry is older than 30 days.
    [path.resolve('./custom-quarantine-reporter.ts')],
  ],
});
```

```typescript
// Annotating quarantined tests with a structured description that the reporter
// can parse — date prefix + tracking URL is the minimum required convention.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Convention: "YYYY-MM-DD: short reason. Tracking: <url>"
// The quarantine reporter extracts the date prefix for SLA calculation.
test.fixme(
  'invoice PDF renders correctly',
  '2026-04-01: PDF renderer hangs on CI Ubuntu runners. Tracking: https://github.com/org/repo/issues/999',
  async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/invoices/123/pdf');
    await expect(page.getByRole('document')).toBeVisible();
  },
);
```

Tradeoff: the `annotation.location` API turns quarantine management from a manual grep exercise into an automated audit trail — every `test.fixme()` now has a machine-readable source location and can be reported, sorted by age, and SLA-checked in CI; the cost is that the feature requires Playwright v1.54 or later, and any annotation added programmatically (e.g., `testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'fixme', description: '...' })`) will have `location: undefined` because there is no static call site to resolve, so the custom reporter must guard against `undefined` location before destructuring (as shown in the code above — `loc?.file ?? '(unknown)'`).

**Pattern 693** — Vitest 4.1 `--detect-async-leaks` With `async_hooks` Source Mapping for Pre-Flakiness Leak Detection  [official]

Vitest 4.1 introduced `--detect-async-leaks` (also `detectAsyncLeaks: true` in config), which uses Node's `async_hooks` to track all async resources (timers, file handles, network sockets, `setInterval` calls) opened during a test and report any that remain open after the test completes. This converts a class of subtle, hard-to-reproduce flakiness — where a test from iteration N leaves an open `setTimeout` that fires during iteration N+1 and corrupts its state — into an immediate, actionable error with a source-mapped stack trace pointing to the exact line that opened the handle.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — enable async leak detection scoped to integration tests
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    // Detect leaked async resources (timers, handles, unresolved promises).
    // WARNING: async_hooks adds ~20–40% overhead to suite wall time.
    // Enable in a dedicated 'leak-check' pipeline rather than every PR run,
    // or scope to the integration test glob where leaks are most likely.
    detectAsyncLeaks: process.env.CHECK_LEAKS === 'true',

    // When a leak is detected, the test is marked as failed with a
    // Vitest-generated error that includes:
    //   - The async resource type (Timeout, TCPSocketWrap, etc.)
    //   - The stack trace at the point the resource was opened
    //   - The test name that opened the resource
    // This is much more actionable than "test sometimes fails" or
    // "Cannot read property of undefined" from downstream corruption.
  },
});
```

```typescript
// Example: a test with a leaked setInterval — common in React component tests
// that start polling on mount but whose cleanup useEffect is never triggered
// because the component is unmounted by the test runner before the effect fires.
import { describe, it, expect, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { render, act } from '@testing-library/react';
import { LiveClock } from '@/components/LiveClock';

describe('LiveClock component', () => {
  // Without --detect-async-leaks: this test passes but the interval from
  // LiveClock's useEffect leaks into the next test, causing random "act()"
  // warnings and occasionally corrupting state in unrelated tests.
  //
  // With --detect-async-leaks: Vitest reports:
  //   LeakDetectedError: Interval (id: 42) opened at LiveClock.tsx:12:5
  //   was not cleared after test 'LiveClock renders current time'
  it('renders current time', () => {
    const { getByRole } = render(<LiveClock />);
    // The component sets up setInterval(updateClock, 1000) on mount.
    // Without cleanup, this interval leaks.
    expect(getByRole('timer')).toBeInTheDocument();
    // FIX: unmount explicitly so the cleanup useEffect fires.
    // The component's useEffect cleanup calls clearInterval(id).
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    // Explicit unmount in afterEach is the correct pattern when the test
    // does not use @testing-library/react's `cleanup` auto-unmount.
    // With @testing-library/react v14+, cleanup() is called automatically
    // after each test — but only if the test uses the render() from the
    // testing-library package directly (not a custom wrapper that bypasses it).
  });
});
```

```typescript
// Recommended: scope --detect-async-leaks to an integration test glob in CI
// by using a separate Vitest project config entry.
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    projects: [
      {
        // Unit tests: no leak detection (fast runs, low leak risk).
        include: ['src/**/*.unit.test.ts'],
        detectAsyncLeaks: false,
      },
      {
        // Integration tests: leak detection enabled.
        // Run with CHECK_LEAKS=true in a nightly pipeline, not every PR.
        include: ['src/**/*.integration.test.ts'],
        detectAsyncLeaks: process.env.CHECK_LEAKS === 'true',
        // Longer timeout to accommodate async_hooks overhead.
        testTimeout: process.env.CHECK_LEAKS === 'true' ? 30_000 : 10_000,
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

Tradeoff: `--detect-async-leaks` catches the single most common source of "ghost flakiness" — where a test passes in isolation but flakes intermittently in parallel runs because a leaked timer from a previous test fires at an unpredictable time — but the async_hooks instrumentation adds 20–40% wall-clock overhead, which makes it impractical as a default on every PR; the correct deployment model is a dedicated nightly "leak sweep" pipeline that runs with `CHECK_LEAKS=true` and posts results as a PR check summary, so that the leak detection signal is systematic (not reactive) without slowing down developer feedback loops; also note that third-party libraries (ORMs, HTTP clients) sometimes open async resources that they legitimately clean up at process exit rather than test exit — these will be reported as leaks even though they are not flakiness sources, so build an allowlist of known-benign resource types (`TCPSocketWrap` from database connection pools, `FSREQCALLBACK` from config file watchers) and filter them from the leak report before acting on it.

### Community Gotchas (continued)

**G257** — `failOnFlakyTests` Blocks CI Even for Pre-Existing Flaky Tests Not Yet Tagged With `test.fixme()`  [community]
Why this matters: when `failOnFlakyTests: true` is enabled in CI for the first time on a suite that already has known-flaky tests, every PR that touches any file is blocked — because the pre-existing flaky tests still retry and flip to "flaky" status on the first CI run after the config change. Teams that enable this without a prior audit end up in a situation where no PR can land until someone marks every pre-existing flaky test with `test.fixme()`, which is a discovery exercise that takes hours and is typically done under merge pressure.
Fix: before enabling `failOnFlakyTests`, run `npx playwright test --repeat-each 5 --reporter json` on a feature branch and parse the output for tests with `"outcome": "flaky"`. Mark each one with `test.fixme('reason: <tracking-url>')`. Only then enable `failOnFlakyTests: true` in the config and merge both changes in the same PR.

**G258** — `locator.describe()` Label Does Not Change Retry or Auto-Wait Behavior — It Is Purely Diagnostic  [community]
Why this matters: developers who discover `locator.describe()` in Playwright v1.53 sometimes assume that giving a locator a descriptive name also changes how Playwright retries it — e.g., "if I describe this as 'lazy-loaded avatar', Playwright will wait longer for it." This is incorrect. `locator.describe()` only affects how the locator appears in trace viewer output and error messages. The actual auto-wait timeout, retry interval, and selector resolution logic are unchanged. A test that was flaky due to a locator resolving before a lazy-loaded element appeared will remain flaky regardless of any `describe()` label applied to it.
Fix: treat `locator.describe()` as a diagnostic annotation layer, not a stability fix. If a locator is flaky because of timing, the correct fix is to add an explicit `waitFor()` or use a more stable semantic locator (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`) that auto-waits for accessibility properties — not to describe the existing flaky locator.

---

### Anti-Patterns (continued)

**AP51** — Running `--detect-async-leaks` on the Full Suite Without Scoping — `async_hooks` Overhead Doubles Suite Wall Time  [anti-pattern]
Mistake: adding `detectAsyncLeaks: true` to the global `vitest.config.ts` without any project scoping or environment guard. On a suite of 800 tests, `async_hooks` instrumentation adds 20–40% overhead per test. A suite that ran in 4 minutes now takes 5.5–6 minutes, and the leak detection signal is diluted by benign resources from ORMs and HTTP clients that are flagged as leaks but are not flakiness sources.
Fix: scope `detectAsyncLeaks` to integration test globs only, guard it behind `process.env.CHECK_LEAKS === 'true'`, and run it in a dedicated nightly pipeline rather than on every PR. Use the `projects` array in `vitest.config.ts` to apply the flag only to the test files where leaks are expected (those hitting real databases, spawning child processes, or using long-lived HTTP connections).

**AP52** — Accessing `annotation.location` Without Guarding Against `undefined` in Custom Reporters  [anti-pattern]
Mistake: a custom reporter that reads `annotation.location.file` (Playwright v1.54+) without checking for `undefined`. Annotations added via `testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'fixme', description: '...' })` in a fixture or `beforeEach` hook have no static call site, so Playwright cannot resolve a source location — `annotation.location` is `undefined`. Destructuring it directly (`const { file, line } = annotation.location`) throws `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'file' of undefined` and crashes the reporter, causing the test run to exit without producing any HTML report.
Fix: always guard: `const loc = annotation.location; const file = loc?.file ?? '(unknown)'; const line = loc?.line ?? 0;`. Additionally, document the convention that quarantine annotations should be added as static `test.fixme()` calls rather than programmatic `testInfo.annotations.push()` — not only for the location metadata, but also because static calls are greppable, visible in `test.only()` runs, and counted by Playwright's built-in `fixme` reporter column.
